title.zh: 卷一百〇六 載記第六 石季龍（石虎）上
title.en: Volume 106 Records 6: Shi Jilong Part One
title.raw: 卷一百〇六 載記第六 石季龍（石虎）上 Volume 106 Records 6: Shi Jilong Part One

sentences.zh: 石季龍[石虎]

translations.literal: Shi Jilong [Shi Hu]
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong (known as Shi Hu)

translations.literal: (First Part)
translations.idiomatic: (Part One)

sentences.zh: 石季龍，勒之從子也，名犯太祖廟諱

translations.literal: Shi Jilong was Shi Le's nephew; his given name violated the temple taboo on the Grand Ancestor's name
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong was a nephew of Shi Le, but his personal name infringed the taboo on the founding emperor's name
(Editorial opening bracket preceding an interpolated gloss.)

sentences.zh: （今注：名石虎，与唐高祖李渊之父李虎同名）〉

translations.literal: (Modern note: His name was Shi Hu, sharing the same written form as Li Hu, father of Tang Gaozu Li Yuan.)>
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: He was named Shi Hu—the graph matches that in Li Hu, father of Tang founder Li Yuan.)>

sentences.zh: ，故稱字焉。

translations.literal: , therefore he was referred to by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: , so he was commonly known by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 祖曰邪，父曰寇覓。

translations.literal: His grandfather was called Ye; his father was called Koumi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather bore the name Ye; his father was Koumi.

sentences.zh: 勒父硃幼而子季龍，故或稱勒弟焉。

translations.literal: Shi Le's father Zhu had adopted Jilong as a son while still a boy, so some called him Shi Le's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shi Le's father Zhu took him in as a son in childhood, people sometimes spoke of him as Shi Le's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 年六七歲，有善相者曰：「此兒貌奇有壯骨，貴不可言。

translations.literal: At six or seven sui, a skilled physiognomist said: "This child's appearance is extraordinary and his bones are strong; his nobility cannot be spoken of."
translations.idiomatic: When he was six or seven, a fortune-teller declared, "The boy's face is strange and his frame powerful—eminence beyond words awaits him."

sentences.zh: 」永興中，與勒相失。

translations.literal: " During the Yongxing era he became separated from Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Yongxing years he was separated from Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 後劉琨送勒母王及季龍于葛陂，時年十七矣。

translations.literal: Later Liu Kun sent Shi Le's mother, Lady Wang, and Jilong to Gebei; at that time he was seventeen sui.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Kun escorted Shi Le's mother Lady Wang and Jilong to Gebei; Jilong was seventeen by then.

sentences.zh: 性殘忍，好馳獵，遊蕩無度，尤善彈，數彈人，軍中以為毒患。

translations.literal: By nature he was cruel and ruthless, fond of galloping and hunting, roaming dissolutely without restraint; he was especially skilled with the sling and repeatedly shot people—within the army he was regarded as a poisonous scourge.
translations.idiomatic: He was vicious by temperament, addicted to the chase and idle roaming, and uncannily good with a sling—he shot men for sport, and the troops deemed him a lethal menace.

sentences.zh: 勒白王將殺之，王曰：「快牛為犢子時，多能破車，汝當小忍之。

translations.literal: Shi Le reported to Lady Wang that he wished to kill him; Lady Wang said: "A spirited ox, while still a calf, often wrecks the cart—you ought to endure him a little."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked Lady Wang's leave to put him to death; she replied, "A mettlesome ox always kicks up trouble as a calf—you must bear with him awhile."

sentences.zh: 」年十八，稍折節。

translations.literal: " At eighteen sui he gradually reformed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " By eighteen he began to curb his ways.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸，趫捷便弓馬，勇冠當時，將佐親戚莫不敬憚，勒深嘉之，拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His height was seven chi five cun; he was agile and handy with bow and horse, and his courage led the age—among commanders, kinsmen, and clients none failed to respect and fear him. Shi Le deeply praised him and appointed him General Who Subdues the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi five cun tall, fleet on horseback and deadly with the bow, and no warrior of the day surpassed him; officers and kin alike dreaded him. Shi Le delighted in him, naming him General Who Subjugates the Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 為娉將軍郭榮妹為妻。

translations.literal: He took as wife the younger sister of General Guo Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He married General Guo Rong's sister.

sentences.zh: 季龍寵惑優僮鄭櫻桃而殺郭氏，更納清河崔氏女，櫻桃又譖而殺之。

translations.literal: Jilong doted on the actor Zheng Yingtao and killed Lady Guo; he then married a daughter of the Boling Cui clan, and Yingtao slandered her as well and had her killed.
translations.idiomatic: Spellbound by the boy actor Zheng Yingtao, he murdered Lady Guo, took a Boling Cui bride, then let Yingtao poison her reputation until she too was executed.

sentences.zh: 所為酷虐。

translations.literal: What he did was cruel and tyrannical.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds were wanton cruelty.

sentences.zh: 軍中有勇幹策略與己俟者，輒方便害之，前後所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Whenever someone in the army matched him in valor, competence, and stratagem, he would find a convenient way to harm him; those he killed before and after were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Any officer whose grit or guile rivaled his own soon met with a convenient accident; the tally of his victims ran high.

sentences.zh: 至於降城陷壘，不復斷別善惡，坑斬士女，鮮有遺類。

translations.literal: As for cities that surrendered or ramparts that fell, he no longer distinguished good from evil—he buried or beheaded men and women alike, and scarcely any survived.
translations.idiomatic: Captured towns brought no mercy: he made no distinction between the innocent and the guilty, slaughtering or entombing civilians until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 勒雖屢加責誘，而行意自若。

translations.literal: Although Shi Le repeatedly reproached and exhorted him, his conduct remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le scolded and cajoled him repeatedly, yet he would not change.

sentences.zh: 然禦眾嚴而不煩，莫敢犯者，指授攻討，所向無前，故勒寵之，信任彌隆，仗以專征之任。

translations.literal: Yet in commanding the masses he was strict without fussiness; none dared transgress his orders. When he directed assaults, nowhere stood before him—therefore Shi Le favored him, trust grew ever deeper, and he was entrusted with sole authority for punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ruled troops with stern clarity that none dared breach, and every campaign he led swept all before him—so Shi Le cherished him, leaned on him ever more, and gave him independent command in the field.

sentences.zh: 季龍徐州從事硃縱殺刺史郭祥，以彭城歸順。

translations.literal: Zhu Zong, an aide in Xuzhou, killed Inspector Guo Xiang and surrendered Pengcheng to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zong, a clerk in Xuzhou, slew Inspector Guo Xiang and handed Pengcheng over to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣將王朗擊之，縱奔淮南。

translations.literal: Jilong sent General Wang Lang to strike him; Zhu fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong dispatched Wang Lang against him; Zhu bolted for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 季龍荒遊廢政，多所營繕，使邃省可尚書奏事，選牧守，祀郊廟；

translations.literal: Jilong abandoned himself to revelry and neglected government, undertaking many construction projects; he had Sui review memorials as provisional overseer of the Masters of Writing, select shepherds and prefects, and sacrifice at the suburban and ancestral temples;
translations.idiomatic: While Jilong roamed in dissipation and left state affairs idle, he piled up building works and ordered Shi Sui to screen petitions for the Masters of Writing, appoint provincial governors, and conduct suburban and temple rites—

sentences.zh: 惟征伐刑斷乃親覽之。

translations.literal: only campaigns, punishments, and judgments did he personally review.
translations.idiomatic: reserving for himself alone decisions on war, criminal law, and verdicts.

sentences.zh: 觀雀台崩，殺典匠少府任汪。

translations.literal: When the Sparrow-Watching Terrace collapsed, he executed Ren Wang, director of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sparrow-Watching Terrace fell, he put Ren Wang, chief of the palace workshops, to death.

sentences.zh: 復使修之，倍于常度。

translations.literal: He ordered it rebuilt on double the usual scale.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded its reconstruction at twice the ordinary dimensions.

sentences.zh: 季龍自率眾南寇曆陽，臨江而旋，京師大震。

translations.literal: Jilong personally led a host south to raid Liyang, halted along the Yangzi, then withdrew, throwing the capital into panic.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong marched south at the head of an army to pillage Liyang, drew up along the Yangzi, and withdrew—leaving the Jin court trembling.

sentences.zh: 遣其征虜石遇寇中廬，遂圍平北將軍桓宣于襄陽。

translations.literal: He dispatched his General Who Subdues the Caitiffs, Shi Yu, to raid Zhonglu and besiege General Who Pacifies the North, Huan Xuan, at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shi Yu, General Who Subdues the Caitiffs, against Zhonglu and penned Huan Xuan, General Who Pacifies the North, inside Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍毛寶、南中郎將王國、征西司馬王愆期等率荊州之眾救之，屯于章山。

translations.literal: General Who Supports the State Mao Bao, General of the Southern Interior Wang Guo, Marshal on the West Expedition Wang Yanqi, and others led Jingzhou forces to relieve them, encamping at Zhang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao, Wang Guo, Wang Yanqi, and other Jin commanders marched Jingzhou troops to the rescue and camped at Zhang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遇攻守二旬，軍中饑疫而還。

translations.literal: Yu attacked and defended for twenty days; famine and plague in the army forced a withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days of fighting left Yu's army starving and plague-stricken, and they fell back.

sentences.zh: 季龍以租入殷廣，轉輸勞煩，令中倉歲入百萬斛，餘皆儲之水次。

translations.literal: Because grain revenues were abundant and transport burdensome, Jilong ordered the central granaries to take in a million hu yearly while storing the surplus at riverside depots.
translations.idiomatic: With rents pouring in and haulage a headache, Jilong capped central intake at a million hu per year and stockpiled the rest along the waterways.

sentences.zh: 晉將軍淳于安攻其琅邪費縣，俘獲而歸。

translations.literal: Jin General Chunyu An attacked his Langye prefecture Fei County, taking captives before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Chunyu An struck Fei county in Langye, carrying off prisoners on his return.

sentences.zh: 石邃保母劉芝初以巫術進，既養邃，遂有深寵，通賄賂，豫言論，權傾朝廷，親貴多出其門，遂封芝為宜城君。

translations.literal: Shi Sui's wet nurse Liu Zhi had first gained entry through sorcery; once she nursed Sui she came under deep favor, took bribes, foretold policy, and tilted power across court—nobles and kin rose mostly through her gate—so Sui ennobled Zhi as Lady of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi, Shi Sui's nurse, had wormed her way in by witchcraft; once she raised the prince she grew irresistible, peddling influence and prophecies until kin and magnates queued at her door—whereupon Sui invested her as Lady of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 季龍下書令刑贖之家得以錢代財帛，無錢聽以穀麥，皆隨時價輸水次倉。

translations.literal: Jilong issued an edict allowing households liable for penal redemption to substitute cash for silk and cloth; those without cash might pay in grain or wheat, all at current prices into the riverside granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong ruled that families buying off punishment could pay coin instead of silk, or grain where coin failed, valued at market rates into the waterfront granaries.

sentences.zh: 冀州八郡雨雹，大傷秋稼，下書深自咎責。

translations.literal: Hailstones struck eight commanderies of Jizhou, devastating the autumn crop; he issued a self-reproaching edict.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Jizhou prefectures were hail-struck and the harvest ruined; he published an edict blaming himself.

sentences.zh: 遣御史所在發水次倉麥，以給秋種，尤甚之處差復一年。

translations.literal: He sent censors to release riverside granary wheat for autumn sowing, remitting a full year's levy in the worst-hit places.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered inspectors to disburse riverside wheat for planting and to waive a year's taxes where damage was severest.

sentences.zh: 季龍將遷于鄴，尚書請太常告廟，季龍曰：「古者將有大事，必告宗廟，而不列社稷。

translations.literal: When Jilong prepared to move the capital to Ye, the Masters of Writing asked the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to announce it at the ancestral temple; Jilong said: "In antiquity, whenever great affairs were imminent, one always informed the ancestral temple but did not rank the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Planning to shift the seat to Ye, the Masters of Writing sought permission for the ritual minister to report at the imperial shrine; Jilong answered, "The old rule was to notify the lineage temple ahead of great undertakings, not the altars of soil and grain."

sentences.zh: 尚書可詳議以聞。

translations.literal: " Let the Masters of Writing deliberate in detail and memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: " Have the Masters of Writing debate this thoroughly and report."

sentences.zh: 」公卿乃請使太尉告社稷，從之。

translations.literal: " The dukes and ministers therefore requested that the Grand Commandant announce it at the altars of soil and grain, and he consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The high ministers then asked the Grand Commandant to proclaim the move at those altars, and Jilong agreed.

sentences.zh: 及入鄴宮，澍雨周洽，季龍大悅，赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: When he entered the Ye palace, soaking rain fell everywhere; Jilong rejoiced greatly and granted amnesty short of capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: As he took possession of the Ye palace, timely rains soaked the realm; overjoyed, he proclaimed amnesty for all but capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 尚方令解飛作司南車成，季龍以其構思精微，賜爵關內侯，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Privy Workshop Director Xie Fei finished a south-pointing carriage; Jilong, marveling at its ingenious design, enfeoffed him as marquis within the passes with lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Workshop chief Xie Fei delivered a south-pointing chariot, Jilong admired its craftsmanship and made him Marquis Within the Passes with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 始制散騎常侍已上得乘軺軒，王公郊祀乘副車，駕四馬，龍旗八旒，塑望朝會即乘軺軒。

translations.literal: For the first time he regulated that Regular Palace Attendants and above might ride light carts; at suburban sacrifices kings and dukes used secondary four-horse carriages with eight-dragon banners, while court assemblies called for light carts.
translations.idiomatic: He first decreed that officials from Regular Palace Attendant upward could ride covered gigs; kings and dukes used secondary four-horse cars with eight pennons at suburban rites, but switched to light gigs for dawn audiences.

sentences.zh: 時羌薄句大猶保險未賓，遣其子章武王斌帥精騎二萬，並秦、雍二州兵以討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang chief Bo Gou-da still held fastnesses and had not submitted; Jilong sent his son, Prince Zhangwu Shi Bin, with twenty thousand picked horsemen plus Bing and Yongzhou troops to chastise him.
translations.idiomatic: While Qiang leader Bo Gou-da clung to redoubts and withheld allegiance, Jilong dispatched Prince Zhangwu Shi Bin at the head of twenty thousand elite horse and forces from Bing and Yong to reduce him.

sentences.zh: 季龍如長樂、衛國，有田疇不辟、桑業不修者，貶其守宰而還。

translations.literal: Jilong toured Changle and Weiguo; wherever fields lay untilled or mulberry culture untended, he degraded the local magistrates before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Changle and Weiguo, he demoted magistrates whose fields lay fallow or whose silk districts languished, then headed home.

sentences.zh: 咸康二年，使牙門將張彌徙洛陽鐘虡、九龍、翁仲、銅駝、飛廉於鄴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiankang he ordered Colonel of the Gates Zhang Mi to relocate from Luoyang the bell racks, Nine Dragons, giant statues, bronze camels, and flying deer icons to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang 2 he assigned Zhang Mi, colonel of the gates, to haul Luoyang's bell-stands, Nine Dragons, colossi, bronze camels, and whirlwind spirits to Ye.

sentences.zh: 鐘一沒於河，募浮沒三百人入河，系以竹絙，牛百頭，鹿櫨引之乃出。

translations.literal: One bell sank in the river; he recruited three hundred divers, tied it with bamboo rope, and used a hundred oxen with windlasses to drag it out.
translations.idiomatic: One bell slipped into the Yellow River; three hundred salvagers with bamboo cables and a hundred oxen on capstans wrestled it ashore.

sentences.zh: 造萬斛舟以渡之，以四輪纏輞車，轍廣四尺，深二尺，運至鄴。

translations.literal: He built ten-thousand-hu barges to ferry them, then four-wheeled rim-wrapped wagons four chi wide in track and two chi deep in rut, and transported everything to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-thousand-hu barges carried the freight; four-wheeled, tire-shod carts—four chi between ruts, two chi deep—rolled the treasure into Ye.

sentences.zh: 季龍大悅，赦二歲刑，賚百官谷帛，百姓爵一級。

translations.literal: Jilong rejoiced greatly, remitted two years of penal labor, rewarded officials with grain and silk, and raised commoners one noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Elated, he waived two years of convict labor, paid officials in grain and cloth, and promoted every commoner one rank.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「三載考績，黜陟幽明，斯則先王之令典，政道之通塞。

translations.literal: An edict declared: "Triennial assessment promotes the obscure and demotes the manifest—such was the statutory model of former kings and the gauge of governance's ease or blockage.
translations.idiomatic: His decree read: "The three-year review that elevates the worthy and casts down the dull was the ancient kings' statute and the touchstone of orderly rule."

sentences.zh: 魏始建九品之制，三年一清定之，雖未盡弘美，亦縉紳之清律，人倫之明鏡。

translations.literal: Wei began the nine-rank system, clarified every third year; though not wholly perfect, it was nonetheless the gentry's clean rule and humanity's bright mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had instituted nine grades and purified them triennially—not flawless, yet the standard that kept the silk-gowned elite honest and reflected moral caliber.

sentences.zh: 從爾以來，遵用無改。

translations.literal: Since then it has been followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since, the realm had accepted it unchanged.

sentences.zh: 先帝創臨天下，黃紙再定。

translations.literal: Our late lord founded the realm and twice fixed ranks on yellow paper.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor began the enterprise and twice certified ranks on yellow edicts.

sentences.zh: 至於選舉，銓為首格。

translations.literal: As for selection and promotion, appraisal ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments, evaluation stood first.

sentences.zh: 自不清定，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Without fresh clarification three years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet three years had slipped by without a new ranking.

sentences.zh: 主者其更銓論，務揚清激濁，使九流咸允也。

translations.literal: Let those in charge reappraise, striving to lift the pure and scour the turbid so that all nine currents find justice.
translations.idiomatic: Responsible ministers must reappraise, championing integrity and purging corruption until every class is satisfied.

sentences.zh: 吏部選舉，可依晉氏九班選制，永為揆法。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel may follow the Jin nine-grade rotation as perpetual statute.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel selection should adhere to the Jin nine-grade rotation as standing law.

sentences.zh: 選畢，經中書、門下宣示三省，然後行之。

translations.literal: When lists are complete, let them be proclaimed through the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery to the three departments before execution.
translations.idiomatic: Once rosters are settled, the Secretariat and Chancellery shall publish them to the three bureaus before enactment.

sentences.zh: 其著此詔書於令。

translations.literal: Inscribe this edict in the ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Engrave this decree in the codified regulations.

sentences.zh: 銓衡不奉行者，御史彈坐以聞。」

translations.literal: Should weighing officials disobey, let the censors impeach and report.
translations.idiomatic: Any registrar who flouts this faces censorial impeachment.

sentences.zh: 索頭郁鞠率眾三萬降于季龍，署鞠等一十三人親通趙王，皆封列侯，散其部眾于冀、青等六州。

translations.literal: Suotou Yuju led thirty thousand followers to surrender to Jilong; Jilong appointed thirteen men including Ju as intimate attendants to the Prince of Zhao, all enfeoffed as full marquises, and dispersed their tribes across six prefectures from Ji to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Suotou chief Yuju brought thirty thousand followers to capitulate; Jilong named thirteen men, Ju among them, as household companions to the Prince of Zhao with columnar marquisates, then scattered their people across Ji, Qing, and four other provinces.

sentences.zh: 時眾役煩興，軍旅不息，加以久旱谷貴，金一斤直米二斗，百姓嗷然無生賴矣。

translations.literal: At that time corvée multiplied without cease and armies marched endlessly; prolonged drought made grain dear—a jin of gold bought but two dou of rice—and the people wailed, left with no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Corvées multiplied, armies never rested, and drought drove grain prices until a pound of gold bought two dou of rice; the populace howled for want of a livelihood.

sentences.zh: 又納解飛之說，于鄴正南投石於河，以起飛橋，功費數千億萬，橋竟不成，役夫饑甚，乃止。

translations.literal: Accepting Xie Fei's scheme, he hurled boulders into the river south of Ye to raise a flying bridge; the works consumed billions yet never spanned the stream—starving laborers forced him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding Xie Fei, he tried to sink stone pylons in the river south of Ye for a soaring bridge; billions vanished and still no span emerged—famished workers made him abandon it.

sentences.zh: 使令長率丁壯隨山津采橡捕魚以濟老弱，而復為權豪所奪，人無所得焉。

translations.literal: He ordered magistrates to lead stalwart youths to mountains and fords for acorns and fish to sustain the aged and weak, yet magnates seized the takings so commoners gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He told prefects to march young men into hills and shallows for acorns and fish to feed elders, but grandees seized every catch, leaving none for the needy.

sentences.zh: 又料殷富之家，配饑人以食之，公卿已下出穀以助振給，奸吏因之侵割無已，雖有貸贍之名而無其實。

translations.literal: He also assessed wealthy households, pairing the starving to devour them; officials down from dukes contributed grain for relief, yet corrupt clerks carved endless graft—though relief was announced in name, none received it in fact.
translations.idiomatic: He assessed rich homes and assigned starvelings to eat them out; ministers donated grain, yet venal clerks skimmed without end—relief existed on paper alone.

sentences.zh: 改直蕩為龍騰，冠以絳幘。

translations.literal: He renamed the Straight Charger guards "Soaring Dragon" and capped them with crimson kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He retitled the Straight Assault guard "Soaring Dragon" and dressed them in scarlet headcloths.

sentences.zh: 于襄國起太武殿，於鄴造東西宮，至是皆就。

translations.literal: He had raised the Grand Martial Hall at Xiangguo and east-west palaces at Ye; by now they stood complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Martial Hall at Xiangguo and twin palaces east and west at Ye were finished at last.

sentences.zh: 太武殿基高二丈八尺，以文石碎之，下穿伏室，置衛士五百人於其中。

translations.literal: The Grand Martial platform rose twenty-eight chi; broken patterned stone paved it, while underground chambers beneath housed five hundred guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Martial podium stood twenty-eight chi high, paved with patterned marble, with vaults below sheltering five hundred sentries.

sentences.zh: 東西七十五步，南北六十五步。

translations.literal: East-west breadth seventy-five paces; north-south sixty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: It measured seventy-five paces east to west and sixty-five north to south.

sentences.zh: 皆漆瓦、金鐺、銀楹、金柱、珠簾、玉壁，窮極枝巧。

translations.literal: Lacquered tiles, gold bells, silver pillars, gold columns, pearl curtains, and jade panels exhausted every artifice.
translations.idiomatic: Lacquered eaves-tiles, gilt chimes, silver jambs, gilded columns, pearl drapes, and jade screens strained every craftsman's wit.

sentences.zh: 又起靈風台九殿于顯陽殿后，選士庶之女以充之。

translations.literal: Behind the Hall of Manifest Yang he built nine Spirit-Wind terraces and drafted commoners' daughters to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Manifest Yang he erected nine Spirit-Wind terraces and pressed daughters of gentry and commoners to people them.

sentences.zh: 後庭服綺縠、玩珍奇者萬餘人，內置女官十有八等，教宮人星占及馬步射。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rear-palace women wore gauze silks and sported curios; eighteen grades of female officers were established, teaching palace ladies astrology and mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand harem women dripped figured silk and rare jewels; eighteen ranks of female administrators taught star lore and horseback shooting.

sentences.zh: 置女太史於靈台，仰觀災祥，以考外太史之虛實。

translations.literal: Female astrologers manned the Spirit Terrace, scanning heaven's omens to check the veracity of the outer observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Women astronomers watched from the Spirit Terrace, charting portents to test the accuracy of the official sky-watchers.

sentences.zh: 又置女鼓吹羽儀，雜伎工巧，皆與外侔。

translations.literal: Female musicians, feathered regalia, and acrobatic troupes matched those outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Female musicians, plumed processions, and variety acts rivaled anything beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 禁郡國不得私學星讖，敢有犯者誅。

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms were forbidden to teach astrology or prophecy privately; offenders faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces could no longer teach star lore or prognostication in secret—violators died.

sentences.zh: 左校令成公段造庭燎於崇杠之末，高十餘丈，上盤置燎，下盤置人，絙繳上下。

translations.literal: Director of the Left Workshops Cheng Gongduan built courtyard beacon-flames atop pole tips more than ten zhang high; upper trays held fuel, lower trays held men, drawn up and down by ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Left Works chief Cheng Gongduan mounted giant torches on masts exceeding ten zhang: fuel burned in the upper basin, men stood in the lower, hoisted on cables.

sentences.zh: 季龍試而悅之。

translations.literal: Jilong tested it and was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong tried the rig and crowed with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 其太保夔安等文武五百九人勸季龍稱尊號，安等方入而庭燎油灌下盤，死者七人。

translations.literal: His Grand Guardian Kui An and five hundred nine civil and military officials urged Jilong to assume an honorific title; as An and the others entered, lamp oil poured onto the lower tray and seven died.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Guardian Kui An led 509 ministers to urge an exalted style upon him, oil cascaded into the lower basin as they approached—seven perished.

sentences.zh: 季龍惡之，大怒，斬成公段於閶闔門。

translations.literal: Jilong considered it ominous, roared with wrath, and executed Cheng Gongduan at the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Reading ill omen in the mishap, Jilong flew into a rage and beheaded Cheng Gongduan at Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 於是依殷周之制，以咸康三年僭稱大趙天王，即位于南郊，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: Thereupon, following Yin-Zhou precedent, in Xiankang three he presumptuously styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao, ascended the throne at the southern suburb, and granted general amnesty short of capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: So, aping Yin and Zhou forms, in Xiankang 3 he arrogated the title Heavenly King of Great Zhao, took the throne south of the capital, and freed all but capital criminals.

sentences.zh: 追尊祖㔨邪為武皇帝，父寇覓為太宗孝皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored grandfather Bei Ye as Martial Emperor and father Koumi as Xiaozong Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized grandfather Bei Ye as Martial Emperor and Koumi as Filial Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 立其鄭氏為天王皇后，以子邃為天王皇太子。

translations.literal: He elevated Lady Zheng as Heavenly Queen and installed son Sui as Heavenly Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Lady Zheng to Heavenly Queen and named Prince Sui Heavenly Heir.

sentences.zh: 親王皆貶封郡公，籓王為縣侯，百官封署各有差。

translations.literal: Princes of the blood were demoted to commandery dukes, cadet kings to county marquises; officials received differentiated titles.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes dropped to commandery dukes, feudal kings to county marquises; the bureaucracy saw reshuffled ranks.

sentences.zh: 太原徙人五百餘戶叛入黑羌。

translations.literal: More than five hundred relocated households from Taiyuan rebelled into the Black Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Over five hundred Taiyuan deportees bolted to join the Black Qiang.

sentences.zh: 武鄉長城徙人韓強獲玄玉璽，方四寸七分，龜紐金文，詣鄴獻之。

translations.literal: Han Qiang, a relocated man from Changcheng in Wuxiang, captured a black jade seal four cun seven fen square with tortoise knob and golden characters and presented it at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qiang, deportee from Changcheng in Wuxiang, seized a black jade seal four cun seven fen on a side—tortoise knob, gilt inscription—and carried it to Ye.

sentences.zh: 拜強騎都尉，復其一門。

translations.literal: He appointed Qiang Colonel of Agile Cavalry and exempted his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang was named Colonel of Agile Cavalry with tax immunity for his clan.

sentences.zh: 夔安等又勸進曰：「臣等謹案大趙水德，玄龜者，水之精也；

translations.literal: Kui An and others pressed further: "We respectfully note that Great Zhao follows the Water virtue; the dark tortoise is Water's essence;
translations.idiomatic: Kui An urged again: Great Zhao holds to Water phase; the black tortoise is Water's quintessence;

sentences.zh: 玉者，石之寶也；

translations.literal: jade is stone's treasure;
translations.idiomatic: jade is stone's treasure;

sentences.zh: 分之數以象七政，寸之紀以准四極。

translations.literal: dividing its measure depicts the Seven Governors; recording its cun aligns with the Four Poles.
translations.idiomatic: its proportions echo the Seven Directors; its cun tally mirrors the Four Extremes.

sentences.zh: 昊天成命，不可久違。

translations.literal: Heaven's completed mandate cannot long be refused.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sealed mandate brooks no delay.

sentences.zh: 輒下史官擇吉日，具禮儀，謹昧死上皇帝尊號。

translations.literal: We therefore instruct the historiographers to choose an auspicious day, prepare ritual, and reverently risk death in offering the imperial style.
translations.idiomatic: Charge the archives to fix an auspicious day, ready the ceremonies, and memorialize the imperial title though it cost our lives.

sentences.zh: 」季龍下書曰：「過相褒美，猥見推逼，覽增恧然，非所望也，其亟止茲議。

translations.literal: Jilong issued an edict: "You praise me excessively and thrust me forward with violence; reading this only deepens my shame—it is not what I hoped for; halt this counsel at once.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong answered, "Your flattery pushes me past bearing; the proposal shames rather than honors me—drop it immediately.

sentences.zh: 今東作告始，自非京城內外，皆不得表慶。

translations.literal: Spring labor now begins; except within the capital, none may submit congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: With spring planting underway, felicitations are forbidden outside the capital."

sentences.zh: 」中書令王波上《玄璽頌》以美之。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Wang Bo presented "Rhapsody on the Dark Seal" to celebrate it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat chief Wang Bo offered an "Ode to the Black Seal" in praise.

sentences.zh: 季龍以石弘時造此璽，強遇而獻之。

translations.literal: Jilong assumed Shi Hong had fashioned this seal and that Qiang merely happened upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong reckoned Shi Hong had forged the seal and Han Qiang stumbled upon it.

sentences.zh: 邃自總百揆之後，荒酒淫色，驕恣無道，或盤游于田，懸管而入，或夜出於宮臣家，淫其妻妾。

translations.literal: After Sui assumed supervision of all affairs, he drowned himself in wine and women, arrogant and lawless—sometimes he hunted until dusk with pipes hung about him, sometimes slipped out by night to ministers' homes and violated their wives.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Sui took the reins, he vanished into wine and women, swaggering beyond law—he hunted till dusk with flutes slung on his back or broke into ministers' houses after dark to rape their wives.

sentences.zh: 妝飾宮人美淑者，斬首洗血，置於盤上，傳共視之。

translations.literal: Among palace women fair and refined he chose some, beheaded them, washed the blood, set the heads on platters, and passed them around for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Pretty maids he decapitated, rinsed the gore, arranged the heads on trays, and circulated them for sport.

sentences.zh: 又內諸比丘尼有姿色者，與其交褻而殺之，合牛羊肉煮而食之，亦賜左右，欲以識其味也。

translations.literal: He also dragged comely Buddhist nuns within the palace to lie with them before killing them, boiled the flesh with ox and mutton, fed it to attendants, and wished them to recognize the flavor.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged attractive nuns into assignations, murdered them, stewed their flesh with beef and mutton, served it to favorites, and demanded they guess the meat.

sentences.zh: 河間公宣、樂安公韜有寵于季龍，邃疾之如仇。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Shi Xuan and Prince of Le'an Shi Tao enjoyed Jilong's favor; Sui hated them like mortal foes.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Prince Xuan of Hejian and Prince Tao of Le'an basked in Jilong's love—Sui loathed them as bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 季龍荒耽內游，威刑失度，邃以事為可呈呈之，季龍恚曰：「此小事，何足呈也。

translations.literal: Jilong abandoned himself to palace wandering and punishments lost proportion; when Sui deemed something worth memorializing he presented it; Jilong angrily said: "This is a small matter—what need is there to present it?"
translations.idiomatic: Lost in harem excess and capricious cruelty, Jilong blew up whenever Shi Sui submitted a report he thought trivial: "Why clutter my desk with this?"

sentences.zh: 」時有所不聞，復怒曰：「何以不呈？

translations.literal: " When sometimes he had not heard of something, he again raged: "Why was it not presented?"
translations.idiomatic: "If news had not reached him, he would rage instead: "Then why didn't you report it?"

sentences.zh: 」誚責杖捶，月至再三。

translations.literal: " He mocked, blamed, and beat him with the cane—several times each month.
translations.idiomatic: "He would jeer, scold, and cane him—sometimes several beatings a month."

sentences.zh: 邃甚恨，私謂常從無窮、長生、中庶子李顏等曰：「官家難稱，吾欲行冒頓之事，卿從我乎？

translations.literal: Sui deeply hated this and privately told his constant attendants Wuqiong, Changsheng, and Household Provisioner Li Yan and others: "The sovereign is impossible to serve; I wish to do what Modu did—will you follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, Shi Sui whispered to Wuqiong, Changsheng, and Li Yan, "Serving this lord is unbearable—I mean to repeat Modu's coup. Are you with me?"

sentences.zh: 」顏等伏不敢對。

translations.literal: " Yan and the others prostrated themselves and dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and could not bring themselves to reply.

sentences.zh: 邃稱疾不省事，率宮臣文武五百餘騎宴于李顏別舍，謂顏等曰：「我欲至冀州殺石宣，有不從者斬！

translations.literal: Sui claimed illness and neglected affairs; leading more than five hundred palace ministers and armed riders he feasted at Li Yan's detached residence and said to Yan and others: "I intend to ride to Jizhou and kill Shi Xuan—whoever refuses shall die!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui feigned sickness, skipped his duties, and rode off with five hundred courtiers to Li Yan's villa, declaring over wine, "I'm marching on Jizhou to murder Shi Xuan—anyone who balks loses his head!"

sentences.zh: 」行數里，騎皆逃散，李顏叩頭固諫，邃亦昏醉而歸。

translations.literal: " After several li the riders had all fled and scattered; Li Yan knocked his head in earnest remonstrance, and Sui, dead drunk, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few miles his escort had melted away; Li Yan begged on his knees until the drunken prince staggered home.

sentences.zh: 邃母鄭氏聞之，私遣中人責邃。

translations.literal: Sui's mother Lady Zheng heard of it and secretly sent an inner attendant to reproach Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng learned of it and dispatched a confidential eunuch to rebuke her son.

sentences.zh: 邃怒，殺其使。

translations.literal: Sui in rage killed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui slew the messenger in a fury.

sentences.zh: 季龍聞邃有疾，遣所親任女尚書察之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Sui was ill, Jilong sent an intimate, Lady Ren of the Masters of Writing, to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Shi Sui sick, Jilong sent the trusted female secretary Ren to inspect him.

sentences.zh: 邃呼前與語，抽劍擊之。

translations.literal: Sui called her forward to speak, then drew a sword and struck her.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui beckoned her close as if to talk, then drew steel and cut her down.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒，收李顏等詰問，顏具言始末，誅顏等三十餘人。

translations.literal: Jilong was furious; he seized Li Yan and others for interrogation; Yan told the whole story from beginning to end; Jilong executed Yan and more than thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong had Li Yan and his circle arrested; under questioning Yan confessed the plot, and thirty-odd men went to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 幽邃於東宮，既而赦之，引見太武東堂。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Sui in the Eastern Palace; afterward he pardoned him and summoned him to an audience at the Grand Martial East Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He locked Shi Sui in the Eastern Palace, then unexpectedly pardoned him and received him at the east hall of the Grand Martial complex.

sentences.zh: 邃朝而不謝，俄而便出。

translations.literal: Sui attended court but did not give thanks; presently he departed directly.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui appeared but offered no thanks and walked straight out.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣使謂邃曰：「太子應入朝中宮，何以便去？

translations.literal: Jilong sent a messenger to say to Sui: "The heir ought to enter court at the empress's palace—why leave directly?"
translations.idiomatic: Jilong sent word: "The crown prince should attend the empress—why bolt away?"

sentences.zh: 」邃逕出不顧。

translations.literal: " Sui went straight out without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui strode off without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒，廢邃為庶人。

translations.literal: Jilong was furious and degraded Sui to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong stripped him of rank and made him a commoner.

sentences.zh: 其夜，殺邃及妻張氏並男女二十六人，同埋於一棺之中。

translations.literal: That night he killed Sui and his wife Lady Zhang together with twenty-six sons and daughters, burying them all in one coffin.
translations.idiomatic: That night he murdered Shi Sui, Lady Zhang, and twenty-six children, stuffing every corpse into a single coffin.

sentences.zh: 誅其宮臣支党二百餘人。

translations.literal: He executed more than two hundred palace ministers and their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Over two hundred of Shi Sui's household faction died with him.

sentences.zh: 廢鄭氏為東海太妃。

translations.literal: He degraded Lady Zheng to Grand Consort of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng was demoted to grand consort of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 立其子宣為天王皇太子，宣母杜昭儀為天王皇后。

translations.literal: He established his son Xuan as Heavenly Crown Prince and Xuan's mother Lady Du the Worthy Consort as Heavenly Queen.
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Xuan heavenly heir and raised Consort Du to heavenly queen.

sentences.zh: 安定人侯子光，弱冠美姿儀，自稱佛太子，從大秦國來，當王小秦國。

translations.literal: Hou Ziguang of Anding, not yet capped, handsome in bearing, called himself the Buddha's crown prince, coming from Daqin to rule Lesser Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Anding, the beardless youth Hou Ziguang—striking looks—proclaimed himself the Buddha's heir from Daqin, destined to king Little Qin.

sentences.zh: 易姓名為李子楊，游於鄠縣爰赤眉家，頗見其妖狀，事微有驗。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Li Ziyang and lodged at Yuan Chimei's home in Hu county; Chimei gradually witnessed his uncanny signs and matters proved somewhat true.
translations.idiomatic: Renaming himself Li Ziyang, he boarded with Yuan Chimei in Hu; omens accumulated until even skeptics admitted something uncanny was afoot.

sentences.zh: 赤眉信敬之，妻以二女，轉相扇惑。

translations.literal: Chimei believed and revered him, married him to two daughters, and they spread delusion from one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Chimei worshipped him, married him both daughters, and the fever spread.

sentences.zh: 京兆樊經、竺龍、嚴諶、謝樂子等聚眾數千人于杜南山，子楊稱大黃帝，建元曰龍興。

translations.literal: Fan Jing, Zhu Long, Yan Chen, Xie Lezi and others of Jingzhao gathered several thousand people at Du South Mountain; Ziyang styled himself Grand Yellow Emperor and established an era title Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jing, Zhu Long, Yan Chen, Xie Lezi, and others raised thousands on Du South Mountain; Li Ziyang declared himself Grand Yellow Emperor with era name Longxing.

sentences.zh: 赤眉與經為左右丞相，龍、諶為左右大司馬，樂子為大將軍。

translations.literal: Chimei and Jing became left and right chancellors; Long and Chen left and right grand marshals; Lezi grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Chimei and Fan Jing took the left and right chancellor seals; Zhu Long and Yan Chen the grand marshal posts; Xie Lezi became commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 鎮西石廣擊斬之。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Shi Guang attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspector Shi Guang rode out and took his head.

sentences.zh: 子楊頸無血，十餘日而面色無異於生。

translations.literal: On Ziyang's neck there was no blood; after more than ten days his complexion was no different from when alive.
translations.idiomatic: No blood pumped from his neck, yet ten days later his face still looked alive—a wonder whispered through the camps.

sentences.zh: 季龍將伐遼西鮮卑段遼，募有勇力者三萬人，皆拜龍騰中郎。

translations.literal: When Jilong prepared to campaign against Duan Liao of the western Liaoxi Xianbei, he recruited thirty thousand men of courage and strength, all appointed Soaring Dragon Household Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilizing against Duan Liao of western Liaoxi, Jilong drafted thirty thousand stalwarts as Soaring Dragon household guards.

sentences.zh: 遼遣從弟屈雲襲幽州，刺史李孟退奔易京。

translations.literal: Liao sent his cousin Qu Yun to raid Youzhou; Inspector Li Meng retreated in flight to Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao sent Qu Yun against Youzhou; Inspector Li Meng fled to the refuge at Yijing.

sentences.zh: 季龍以桃豹為橫海將軍，王華為渡遼將軍，統舟師十萬出漂渝津，支雄為龍驤大將軍，姚弋仲為冠軍將軍，統步騎十萬為前鋒，以伐段遼。

translations.literal: Jilong appointed Tao Bao General Who Spans the Seas and Wang Hua General Who Crosses the Liao, commanding a hundred thousand naval troops out from Piaoyu Ford; Zhi Xiong as Grand General Who Soars Like a Dragon and Yao Yizhong as General Who Vanquishes the Vanguard, commanding a hundred thousand infantry and horse as vanguard, to attack Duan Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Bao and Wang Hua led a hundred thousand sailors from Piaoyu; Zhi Xiong and Yao Yizhong marched another hundred thousand overland—the pincer aimed at Duan Liao.

sentences.zh: 季龍眾次金台，支雄長驅入薊，遼漁陽太守馬鮑、代相張牧、北平相陽裕、上谷相侯龕等四十餘城並率眾降于季龍。

translations.literal: Jilong's host halted at Golden Terrace; Zhi Xiong drove deep into Ji; Liao's Administrator of Yuyang Ma Bao, Chancellor of Dai Zhang Mu, Chancellor of Beiping Yang Yu, Chancellor of Shanggu Hou Kan and more than forty cities all led their masses to surrender to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Golden Terrace, Zhi Xiong plunged into Ji; forty-some cities—Yuyang, Dai, Beiping, Shanggu—opened their gates to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 支雄攻安次，斬其部大夫那樓奇。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiong attacked Anci and beheaded their senior official Nalou Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong stormed Anci and struck down minister Nalou Qi.

sentences.zh: 遼懼，棄令支，奔於密雲山。

translations.literal: Liao feared, abandoned Lingzhi, and fled to Miyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Panicking, Duan Liao abandoned Lingzhi for Miyun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遼右左長史劉群、盧諶、司馬崔悅等封其府庫，遣使請降。

translations.literal: Liao's senior scribes Liu Qun, Lu Chen, and clerk Cui Yue sealed the government treasuries and sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerks Liu Qun and Lu Chen, with Cui Yue, sealed the vaults and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣將軍郭太、麻秋等輕騎二萬追遼，及之，戰於密雲，獲其母妻，斬級三千。

translations.literal: Jilong sent Generals Guo Tai and Ma Qiu with twenty thousand light horse in pursuit; overtaking him they fought at Miyun, captured his mother and wives, and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai and Ma Qiu raced after him with twenty thousand light horse, fought at Miyun, seized his womenfolk, and piled three thousand skulls.

sentences.zh: 遼單馬竄險，遣子乞特真送表及名馬，季龍納之。

translations.literal: Liao fled alone on horseback into defiles and sent his son Qitezhen to deliver a memorial and famous horses; Jilong accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao bolted alone into the ravines while his son Qitezhen carried tribute horses and a surrender memorial—Jilong accepted.

sentences.zh: 乃遷其戶二萬餘于雍、司、兗、豫四州之地，諸有才行者皆擢敘之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he relocated more than twenty thousand households to the territories of Yong, Si, Yan, and Yu prefectures, promoting all who had talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand households went to Yong, Si, Yan, and Yu; anyone with merit earned promotion.

sentences.zh: 先是，北單于乙回為鮮卑敦那所逐，既平遼西，遣其將李穆擊那破之，復立乙回而還。

translations.literal: Earlier the Northern Chanyu Yihui had been driven out by Xianbei Dunduo; after pacifying western Liaoxi he sent General Li Mu to strike Dunduo and defeat him, restored Yihui, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, Northern Chanyu Yihui had fled Xianbei Dunduo; once Liaoxi fell, Li Mu smashed Dunduo and reinstated Yihui.

sentences.zh: 季龍入遼宮，論功封賞各有差。

translations.literal: Jilong entered Liao's palace and discussed merits, enfeoffing and rewarding each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong toured Duan Liao's halls and handed out fiefs by merit.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容皝與段遼有隙，遣使稱籓于季龍，陳遼宜伐，請盡眾來會。

translations.literal: Earlier Murong Huang had been at odds with Duan Liao; he sent envoys declaring submission to Jilong, arguing Liao should be attacked and requesting to bring all his troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang, long estranged from Duan Liao, had pledged allegiance to Zhao and urged a joint strike.

sentences.zh: 及軍至令支，皝師不出，季龍將伐之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Lingzhi, Huang's army did not emerge; Jilong prepared to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingzhi the Yan army never showed; Jilong ready his wrath against Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 天竺佛圖澄進曰：「燕福德之國，未可加兵。

translations.literal: Fotucheng of Tianzhu advanced comment: "Yan is a land of fortune's virtue—do not apply arms."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fotucheng warned, "Yan enjoys heaven's favor—do not send blades there."

sentences.zh: 」季龍作色曰：「以此攻城，何城不克？

translations.literal: " Jilong changed color and said: "With this I assault cities—what city would not fall?
translations.idiomatic: Jilong flushed: "With such hosts I could crack any wall."

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，誰能禦之？

translations.literal: With this host in battle, who could withstand them?
translations.idiomatic: Who could stand against this army in the field?

sentences.zh: 區區小豎，何所逃也？

translations.literal: How could that petty stripling escape?
translations.idiomatic: That stripling cannot slip away.

sentences.zh: 」太史令趙攬固諫曰：「燕城歲星所守，行師無功，必受其禍。

translations.literal: " Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan firmly remonstrated: "The Yan capital stands where the Year Star guards—campaigning brings no success and will surely bring disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Grand astrologer Zhao Lan insisted: "The Year Star watches Yan—strike there and heaven punishes you."

sentences.zh: 」季龍怒，鞭之，黜為肥如長。

translations.literal: " Jilong raged, flogged him, and demoted him to magistrate of Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong had him whipped and busted down to magistrate of Feiru.

sentences.zh: 進師攻棘城，旬餘不克。

translations.literal: He advanced the army to assault Ji city; after more than ten days it did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Ji dragged past ten days without breach.

sentences.zh: 皝遣子恪帥胡騎二千，晨出挑戰，諸門皆若有師出者，四面如雲，季龍大驚，棄甲而遁。

translations.literal: Huang sent son Ke leading two thousand Hu horse out at dawn to challenge; at every gate it seemed as if forces were issuing—cloudlike on four sides—Jilong was greatly alarmed, cast off armor, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke sortied at dawn with two thousand Hu horse; phantom banners sprouted at every gate until Zhao's host broke and Jilong threw away harness and ran.

sentences.zh: 於是召趙攬復為太史令。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Zhao Lan back to Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened, he recalled Zhao Lan as court astrologer.

sentences.zh: 季龍旋自令支，過易京，惡其固而毀之。

translations.literal: Jilong rotated back from Lingzhi, passed Yijing, detested its strength and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Marching home via Lingzhi, he razed Yijing out of spite for its stubborn walls.

sentences.zh: 還謁石勒墓，朝其群臣于襄國建德前殷，復從征文武有差。

translations.literal: Returning he visited Shi Le's tomb and held court for his ministers before the Jiande Front Hall at Xiangguo; civil and military followers of the campaign received differentiated rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He paused at Shi Le's tomb, convened his ministers before Xiangguo's Jiande Front Hall, and graded rewards for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 至鄴，設飲至之禮，賜俘偏于丞郎。

translations.literal: At Ye he held the Victors' Feast ritual and distributed captives among assistants and masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye he staged the victors' banquet and parceled captives among secretariat aides.

sentences.zh: 季龍謀伐昌黎，遣渡遼曹伏將青州之眾渡海，戍蹋頓城，無水而還，因戍於海島，運谷三百萬斛以給之。

translations.literal: Jilong planned to campaign against Changli; he sent Crossing-Liao Cao Fu to lead Qingzhou forces across the sea to garrison Tadun city; finding no water they returned, then garrisoned on sea islands, shipping three million hu of grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: For Changli he ordered Cao Fu to ferry Qingzhou troops to Tadun; wells failed, so they held sea islands while three million hu of grain sailed out to feed them.

sentences.zh: 又以船三百艘運穀三十萬斛詣高句麗，使典農中郎將王典率眾萬餘屯田于海濱。

translations.literal: He also used three hundred ships to transport three hundred thousand hu of grain to Goguryeo and ordered Household Farming Household-General Wang Dian to lead more than ten thousand to farm colonies on the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred ships carried another three hundred thousand hu toward Goguryeo while Wang Dian planted ten thousand colonists along the coast.

sentences.zh: 又令青州造船千艘。

translations.literal: He also ordered Qingzhou to build a thousand ships.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou's yards laid keels for a thousand hulls.

sentences.zh: 使石宣率步騎二萬擊朔方鮮卑斛摩頭破之，斬首四萬餘級。

translations.literal: He sent Shi Xuan with twenty thousand infantry and horse to strike Shuofang Xianbei Humotou and defeat him, taking more than forty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan shattered Shuofang Xianbei Humotou with twenty thousand men and stacked forty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 冀州八郡大蝗，司隸請坐守宰，季龍曰：「此政之失和，朕之不德，而欲委咎守宰，豈禹、湯罪己之義邪！

translations.literal: Eight commanderies of Jizhou suffered great locusts; the Metropolitan Governor requested to punish magistrates; Jilong said: "This is disharmony in governance and lack of virtue on Our part—yet you would blame magistrates—how does that match the meaning by which Yu and Tang blamed themselves!
translations.idiomatic: Locusts devoured eight Jizhou circuits; when the capital governor demanded magistrates' heads, Jilong answered, "Policy failed—the fault is mine. Would Yu and Tang have blamed their prefects?"

sentences.zh: 司隸不進讜言，佐朕不逮，而歸咎無辜，所以重吾之責，可白衣領司隸。」

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor did not advance loyal words to aid Our shortcomings but blamed the guiltless—thereby doubling Our fault—he may wear plain clothes while acting as Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: You offer no loyal counsel yet punish innocents—doubling my shame. Serve as metropolitan governor in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 加其子司徒韜金鉦黃鉞，鑾輅九旒。

translations.literal: He added to his son Minister of Education Shi Tao golden cymbals and yellow battle-axe, imperial carriage with nine banners.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Tao, minister of education, received golden cymbals, yellow axe, and a nine-banner imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 先是，使襄城公涉歸、上庸公日歸率眾戍長安，二歸告鎮西石廣私樹恩澤，潛謀不軌。

translations.literal: Earlier he had ordered Princes Shegui of Xiangcheng and Rigui of Shangyong to lead hosts garrisoning Chang'an; the two Rigui reported that Regional Inspector Shi Guang was privately cultivating favor and secretly plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Shegui and Rigui, holding Chang'an, accused Shi Guang of buying loyalty and plotting sedition.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒，追廣至鄴，殺之。

translations.literal: Jilong was furious, summoned Guang to Ye, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong recalled Guang to Ye and executed him.

sentences.zh: 段遼於密雲山遣使詐降，季龍信之，使征東麻秋百里郊迎，敕秋曰：「受降如待敵，將軍慎之。

translations.literal: Duan Liao at Miyun Mountain sent envoys feigning surrender; Jilong believed them and ordered Eastern Expedition Ma Qiu to greet him a hundred li from the suburbs; he instructed Qiu: "Receiving surrender is like awaiting the enemy—general, be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao's sham surrender duped Jilong into ordering Ma Qiu to escort him—a hundred li out—with the warning, "Treat a capitulation like an ambush."

sentences.zh: 」遼又遣使降于慕容皝曰：「胡貪而無謀，吾今請降求迎，彼終不疑也。

translations.literal: " Liao again sent envoys surrendering to Murong Huang saying: "The Hu are greedy and without stratagem; I now ask to surrender and seek escort—they will never suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Duan Liao messaged Murong Huang: "Those barbarians are greedy and dull; if I beg escort they will never smell the trap."

sentences.zh: 若伏重軍以要之，可以得志。

translations.literal: If you lay heavy troops in ambush to await them, you can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Lay a cordon of veterans and you will break them."

sentences.zh: 」皝遣子恪伏兵於密雲。

translations.literal: " Huang sent son Ke to lay ambush at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang hid Murong Ke at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 麻秋統眾三萬迎遼，為恪所襲，死者十六七，秋步遁而歸。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu commanded thirty thousand to welcome Liao; Ke ambushed him—sixty or seventy percent died; Qiu fled on foot and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu marched thirty thousand into Murong Ke's teeth; six or seven parts died; Qiu limped home alone.

sentences.zh: 季龍聞之驚怒，方食吐餔，乃削秋官爵。

translations.literal: Hearing this Jilong was shocked and furious; just as he was eating he vomited his meal—thereupon he stripped Qiu of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The news hit Jilong mid-meal—he vomited and stripped Ma Qiu of every rank.

sentences.zh: 下書令諸郡國立五經博士。

translations.literal: He issued an edict ordering every commandery and kingdom to establish doctoral chairs for the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded each province to appoint professors for the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 初，勒置大小學博士，至是復置國子博士、助教。

translations.literal: Earlier Shi Le had placed doctoral chairs for greater and lesser schools; now he again placed doctoral chairs and assistants for the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's old minor and major academy chairs now gained imperial-academy assistants under Jilong.

sentences.zh: 季龍以吏部選舉斥外耆德，而勢門童幼多為美官，免郎中魏ＫＪ為庶人。

translations.literal: Jilong found that Ministry appointments excluded aged worthies while sons of powerful houses mostly held fine offices; he dismissed Gentleman-of-the-Palace Wei [graphs damaged in transmitted text] to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that personnel posts went to boys from great houses while graybeards languished, he cashiered Palace Gentleman Wei—whose name is corrupted in the text—to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 以其太子宣為大單于，建天子旌旗。

translations.literal: He appointed Crown Prince Xuan Grand Chanyu and established imperial banners as for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shi Xuan became Grand Chanyu with banners reserved for emperors.

sentences.zh: 以夔安為征討大都督，統五將步騎七萬寇荊揚北鄙。

translations.literal: He appointed Kui An Grand Commander for Punitive Expeditions, commanding five generals with seventy thousand infantry and horse to raid the northern marches of Jing and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui An led five generals and seventy thousand men against Jin's northern Jing-Yang frontier.

sentences.zh: 石閔敗王師于沔陰，將軍蔡懷死之。

translations.literal: Shi Min defeated the imperial army at Yinyin; General Cai Huai died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min shattered the Jin host at Yinyin; Cai Huai fell.

sentences.zh: 宣將硃保又敗王師于白石，將軍鄭豹、談玄、郝莊、隨相、蔡熊皆遇害。

translations.literal: Xuan's general Zhu Bao again defeated the imperial army at Baishi; Generals Zheng Bao, Tan Xuan, Hao Zhuang, Sui Xiang, and Cai Xiong all met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bao, under Shi Xuan, crushed another imperial corps at Baishi; Zheng Bao, Tan Xuan, Hao Zhuang, Sui Xiang, and Cai Xiong died.

sentences.zh: 季龍將張賀度攻陷邾城，敗晉將毛寶於邾西，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Jilong's general Zhang Hedu's assault took Zhu city and defeated Jin general Mao Bao west of Zhu—more than ten thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedu seized Zhu city and broke Mao Bao west of the walls—ten thousand Jin dead.

sentences.zh: 夔安進據胡亭，晉將軍黃沖、曆陽太守鄭進皆降之。

translations.literal: Kui An advanced and seized Huting; Jin General Huang Chong and Administrator of Liyang Zheng Jin both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kui An took Huting; Huang Chong and Liyang's Zheng Jin capitulated.

sentences.zh: 安於是掠七萬戶而還。

translations.literal: An thereupon plundered seventy thousand households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy thousand households went north as booty.

sentences.zh: 時豪戚侵恣，賄托公行，季龍患之，擢殿中御史李矩為御史中丞，特親任之。

translations.literal: At that time magnate kin encroached wantonly and bribery ran openly; Jilong worried over it and promoted Palace Censor Li Ju to Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief with special trust.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of the great houses seized fields and sold offices until Jilong elevated palace censor Li Ju to palace vice-censor with carte blanche.

sentences.zh: 自此百僚震懾，州郡肅然。

translations.literal: From this the hundred officials trembled and prefectures and commanderies stood in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Officials froze; provinces snapped to attention.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「朕聞良臣如猛獸，高步通衢而豺狼避路，信矣哉！」

translations.literal: Jilong said: "We have heard that good ministers are like fierce beasts—striding the high road while wolves give way—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: Jilong mused, "They say a righteous minister is a tiger on the highway—wolves scatter ahead of him. True enough!"

sentences.zh: 鎮遠王擢表雍、秦二州望族，自東徙已來，遂在戍役之例，既衣冠華胄，宜蒙優免，從之。

translations.literal: Regional Defender Wang Zhuo memorialized that elite clans of Yong and Qin prefectures, since eastward migration, had fallen under corvée rules; as they're cap-and-gown nobility they should receive exemption—he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo argued that Yong and Qin's old elite, dragged east, deserved exemption from soldier rolls as cultivated houses—Jilong agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是皇甫、胡、梁、韋、杜、牛、辛等十有七姓蠲其兵貫，一同舊族，隨才銓敘，思欲分還桑梓者聽之；

translations.literal: Thereafter seventeen surnames including Huangfu, Hu, Liang, Wei, Du, Niu, and Xin were released from military registers and treated like old clans; according to talent they were ranked; those who wished to divide and return to native places were permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen lineages—Huangfu, Hu, Liang, Wei, Du, Niu, Xin, and the rest—left the conscription lists like ancient nobility; talent decided appointments; anyone wishing to go home could.

sentences.zh: 其非此等，不得為例。

translations.literal: those not of this group might not take it as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Others could cite no such privilege.

sentences.zh: 以其撫軍李農為使持節、監遼西北平諸軍事、征東將軍、營州牧，鎮令支。

translations.literal: He appointed his Army-Soothing Li Nong commissioner with baton, supervisor of military affairs of Liaoxi and Beiping, General Who Conquers the East, and shepherd of Yingzhou, garrisoning Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong became commissioner with baton, overseer of Liaoxi-Beiping armies, eastern conqueror, Yingzhou shepherd, stationed at Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 于時大旱，白虹經天，季龍下書曰：「朕在位六載，不能上和乾象，下濟黎元，以致星虹之變。

translations.literal: At that time great drought prevailed and a white rainbow spanned heaven; Jilong issued an edict: "We have held the throne six years yet cannot harmonize celestial signs above or succor the black-haired folk below, bringing mutations of stars and rainbows.
translations.idiomatic: Drought seared the realm and a white rainbow arched the sky; Jilong confessed six fruitless years that offended heaven and starved the people.

sentences.zh: 其令百僚各上封事，解西山之禁，蒲葦魚鹽除歲供之外，皆無所固。

translations.literal: Let the hundred officials each submit sealed memorials; lift prohibitions on western hills; reeds, rushes, fish, and salt beyond yearly tribute shall none be monopolized.
translations.idiomatic: He invited sealed criticism, opened western hills to fuel gathering, and forbade monopolies on reed, fish, or salt beyond statutory tribute.

sentences.zh: 公侯卿牧不得規占山澤，奪百姓之利。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, ministers, and shepherds may not scheme to occupy mountains and marshes and seize profit from the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: No duke, minister, or governor might fence off marshes or hills against commoners.

sentences.zh: 」又下書曰：「前以豐國、澠池二冶初建，徙刑徒配之，權救時務。

translations.literal: " He again issued an edict: "Earlier because the Fengguo and Mianchi foundries were first established, relocated convicts were assigned—temporarily to meet the times.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict admitted that assigning convicts to new Fengguo and Mianchi smelters had been an emergency measure.

sentences.zh: 而主者循為恆法，致起怨聲。

translations.literal: Yet overseers treated it as standing practice, raising cries of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats froze it into permanent labor, sparking outrage.

sentences.zh: 自今罪犯流徒，皆當申奏，不得輒配也。

translations.literal: From now criminals sentenced to exile must each be memorialized—none may be assigned without approval.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every exile requires imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 京獄見囚，非手殺人，一皆原遣。

translations.literal: Prisoners currently in the capital jail who did not kill with their own hands shall one and all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Capital inmates who killed no one directly go free.

sentences.zh: 」其日澍雨。

translations.literal: " That day soaking rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Rain soaked the capital that same day.

sentences.zh: 季龍將討慕容皝，令司、冀、青、徐、幽、、並、雍兼復之家五丁取三。

translations.literal: When Jilong prepared to campaign against Murong Huang he ordered that in Si, Ji, Qing, Xu, You, Bing, Yong, and households liable for double military obligation, three of every five adult males be levied.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilizing against Murong Huang, he took three of every five fit men from Si, Ji, Qing, Xu, You, Bing, Yong, and families liable for double service.

sentences.zh: 四丁取二，合鄴城舊軍滿五十萬，具船萬艘，自河通海，運穀豆千一百萬斛于安樂城，以備征軍之調。

translations.literal: Two from every four; combined with Ye's standing army to fill five hundred thousand; equipped ten thousand ships; from the river through the sea transported eleven million hu of grain and beans to Anle city to supply requisition for the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere two of four were pressed; with Ye's existing troops the roll reached half a million; ten thousand hulls moved eleven million hu of grain and beans by river and sea to Anle for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 徙遼西、北平、漁陽萬戶於兗、豫、雍、洛四州之地。

translations.literal: He relocated ten thousand households from western Liaoxi, Beiping, and Yuyang to Yan, Yu, Yong, and Luo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand households from western Liaoxi, Beiping, and Yuyang resettled in Yan, Yu, Yong, and Luo.

sentences.zh: 季龍僭位之後，有所調用，皆選司擬官，經令僕而後奏行。

translations.literal: After Jilong's usurpation of title, whenever there were appointments the Selection Bureau drafted nominees, passing through Commandant and Supervisor before memorializing execution.
translations.idiomatic: Since claiming the throne, appointments flowed Selection Bureau → commandant → supervisor → throne.

sentences.zh: 不得其人，案以為令僕之負，尚書及郎不坐。

translations.literal: When the person was unsuitable, it was filed as the Commandant's or Supervisor's fault—the Masters of Writing and gentlemen did not bear blame.
translations.idiomatic: Bad picks blamed left/right directors—not the ministry rank-and-file.

sentences.zh: 至是，吏部尚書劉真以為失銓考之體而言之，季龍責怒主者，加真光祿大夫，金章紫綬。

translations.literal: By now Minister of Personnel Liu Zhen deemed this a violation of appraisal norms and spoke of it; Jilong rebuked those responsible and promoted Zhen to Household Grandee with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel chief Liu Zhen protested that this gutted evaluation rites; Jilong punished the overseers and ennobled Zhen as household grandee with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 季龍如宛陽，大閱於曜武場。

translations.literal: Jilong went to Wanyang and held a grand review at the Yaowu parade ground.
translations.idiomatic: At Wanyang Jilong staged a full-dress military review on the Field of Glorious Arms.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝襲幽、冀，略三萬餘家而去。

translations.literal: Murong Huang raided You and Ji, carrying off more than thirty thousand households before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang swept through You and Ji, uprooting thirty thousand families before riding away.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史石光坐懦弱征還。

translations.literal: Inspector of You Shi Guang was impeached for cowardice and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou inspector Shi Guang lost his post for spinelessness and was summoned home.

sentences.zh: 賜征士辛謐几杖衣服，穀五百斛，敕平原為起甲第。

translations.literal: He bestowed on recluse scholar Xin Mi an armrest, staff, and robes plus five hundred hu of grain, ordering Pingyuan to raise for him a walled mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The hermit Xin Mi received cane, armrest, clothes, and five hundred hu of grain; Jilong told Pingyuan to build him a noble compound.

sentences.zh: 先是，李壽將李宏自晉奔于季龍，壽致書請之，題曰趙王石君。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Shou's general Li Hong had fled from Jin to Jilong; Shou sent a letter requesting his return, addressing it to "Lord Shi, Prince of Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong of Cheng Han had defected from Jin to Zhao; Li Shou wrote asking him back, superscribing the envelope to "Prince of Zhao, Lord Shi."

sentences.zh: 季龍不悅，付外議之，多有異同。

translations.literal: Jilong was displeased and handed it to outer court deliberation; opinions varied greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The superscription irked Jilong; court debate split.

sentences.zh: 中書監王波議曰：「今李宏以死自誓，若得反魂蜀漢，當鳩率宗族，混同王化。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Supervisor Wang Bo argued: "Now Li Hong pledges himself unto death; if he may revive his soul in Shu-Han, he will rally his lineage and merge into royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo urged: "Li Hong swears himself to death—yet if he lives to stir Shu-Han, his clan might submit to your sway.

sentences.zh: 若遣而果也，則不煩一旅之師而坐定梁、益，就有進退，豈在逃命一夫。

translations.literal: If we send him back and he proves true, then without tiring a single brigade we sit and settle Liang and Yi; whatever advance or retreat follows, how does it hinge on one fleeing man?
translations.idiomatic: Should he prove loyal once returned, Liang and Yi fall without a campaign; gain or loss thereafter hardly rests on one refugee.

sentences.zh: 壽既號並日月，跨僭一方，今若制詔，或敢酬反，則取誚戎裔。

translations.literal: Shou already styles himself co-equal with sun and moon and straddles a corner in usurpation—if we now issue an imperial rescript, he may dare an insulting reply and invite ridicule from frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou already pairs himself with heaven—bold usurpation—so an imperial tone might earn a sneering answer and shame among border peoples.

sentences.zh: 宜書答之，並贈以楛矢，使壽知我遐荒必臻也。

translations.literal: We ought answer by letter and moreover gift hawthorn arrows, letting Shou know our distant wilds surely arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Better reply in kind and send hawthorn arrows—the classical tribute of far tribes—so Shou sees Zhao's reach.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣宏，備物以酬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Hong back with goods to reciprocate.
translations.idiomatic: He released Li Hong laden with return gifts.

sentences.zh: 以石韜為太尉，與太子宣迭日省可尚書奏事。

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Tao Grand Commandant to alternate days with Crown Prince Xuan in reviewing memorials for the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao became grand commandant, sharing alternate days with Shi Xuan screening petitions for the ministry.

sentences.zh: 自幽州東至白狼，大興屯田。

translations.literal: From Youzhou east to Bailang he massively expanded military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: East from Youzhou to Bailang he poured labor into frontier farms.

sentences.zh: 張駿憚季龍之盛，遣其別駕馬詵朝之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun feared Jilong's might and sent his Clerk Ma Shen to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun of Former Liang, dreading Zhao's strength, dispatched aide Ma Shen to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 季龍初大悅，及覽其表，辭頗蹇傲，季龍大怒，將斬詵。

translations.literal: Jilong was at first greatly pleased, but when he read the memorial its wording was rather stiff and proud; Jilong was furious and prepared to execute Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Delight turned to rage when Ma Shen's memorial read arrogant—Jilong reached for the headsman's sword.

sentences.zh: 侍中石璞進曰：「為陛下之患者，丹陽也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shi Pu advanced comment: "What troubles Your Majesty is Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Shi Pu murmured, "Your real foe sits in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 區區河右，焉能為有無！

translations.literal: How could the petty river west matter either way!
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi corridor is a sideshow.

sentences.zh: 今斬馬詵，必征張駿，則南討之師勢分為二，建鄴君臣延其數年之命矣。

translations.literal: Now if we behead Ma Shen we must surely campaign against Zhang Jun—then forces for the southern expedition split in two and the court at Jianye buys itself several more years of life.
translations.idiomatic: Kill Ma Shen and you march on Liang—splitting the army meant for the south and gifting Jianye extra seasons.

sentences.zh: 勝之不為武，弗克為四夷所笑，不如因而厚之。

translations.literal: Victory would not prove martial prowess; failure would make the four barbarians laugh—it is better therefore to treat him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Victory proves little; defeat makes barbarians mock—better pamper him.

sentences.zh: 彼若改圖謝罪，率其臣職者，則我又何求！

translations.literal: If he should alter course, apologize for crimes, and lead his ministers in duty—what more would we seek!
translations.idiomatic: Should he mend his tone and resume vassalage, we need nothing more.

sentences.zh: 迷而不悟，討之未後也。

translations.literal: If he remains lost without awakening, punishing him later is not too late.
translations.idiomatic: If he stays blind, we can strike later.

sentences.zh: 」季龍乃止。

translations.literal: " Jilong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 李宏既至蜀漢，李壽欲誇其境內，下令云：「羯使來庭，獻其楛矢。

translations.literal: After Hong reached Shu-Han, Li Shou wished to boast within his borders and issued an order saying: "Envoys of the Jie have come to court and presented their hawthorn arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Hong arrived, Li Shou bragged that "barbarian envoys" had brought classic hawthorn shafts.

sentences.zh: 」季龍聞之怒甚，黜王波以白衣守中書監。

translations.literal: " Hearing this Jilong was furious beyond measure and demoted Wang Bo to supervise the Palace Secretariat in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The boast enraged Jilong; Wang Bo kept his portfolio only as a humiliated officer in undyed robes.

sentences.zh: 季龍志在窮兵，以其國內少馬，乃禁畜私馬，匿者腰斬，收百姓馬四萬餘匹以入於公。

translations.literal: Jilong's ambition aimed at exhausting armies; because horses were scarce domestically he forbade private horse breeding—those who concealed horses were cut at the waist—and confiscated more than forty thousand commoners' horses for the public herds.
translations.idiomatic: Determined to fight forever and short of mounts, he banned private horses—hidden stock meant waist execution—and seized forty thousand civilian animals for the state.

sentences.zh: 兼盛興宮室於鄴，起台觀四十餘所，營長安、洛陽二宮，作者四十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Concurrently he lavishly raised palace structures at Ye, erecting more than forty terraces and lookout towers, and built twin palaces at Chang'an and Luoyang—four hundred thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Ye sprouted forty-plus towers; Chang'an and Luoyang gained new palaces—four hundred thousand builders.

sentences.zh: 又敕河南四州具南師之備，並、朔、秦、雍嚴四討之資，青、冀、幽州三五發卒，諸州造甲者五十萬人。

translations.literal: He also ordered the four southern Henan prefectures to prepare against southern armies, Bing, Shuo, Qin, and Yong to tighten stores for four-direction expeditions, Qing, Ji, and You to levy men on three-or-five schedules, and fifty thousand armorer households across the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's south rim readied anti-Jin defenses; Bing, Shuo, Qin, Yong stockpiled northern campaigns; Qing, Ji, You drafted men by the three-in-five rule; fifty thousand smiths forged armor.

sentences.zh: 兼公侯牧宰競興私利，百姓失業，十室而七。

translations.literal: Together dukes, marquises, shepherds, and magistrates vied for private profit until commoners lost livelihood—seven in ten households ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Magnates skimmed contracts until seven tenths of homes collapsed.

sentences.zh: 船夫十七萬人為水所沒、猛獸所害，三分而一。

translations.literal: One hundred seventy thousand boatmen drowned or were taken by beasts—a third perished.
translations.idiomatic: One third of a hundred seventy thousand boatmen drowned or fed river monsters.

sentences.zh: 貝丘人李弘因眾心之怨，自言姓名應讖，遂連結奸黨，署置百僚。

translations.literal: Li Hong of Beiqu, exploiting popular resentment, declared his name matched prophecy, then linked a cabal and appointed a full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: In Beiqu, Li Hong rode popular hate, claimed destiny chose his name, knotted a conspiracy, and named ministers.

sentences.zh: 事發，誅之，連坐者數千家。

translations.literal: When the affair broke he executed them; those implicated by association numbered several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Exposure brought mass execution—thousands of families caught in the net.

sentences.zh: 季龍畋獵無度，晨出夜歸，又多微行，躬察作役之所。

translations.literal: Jilong hunted without measure, going out at dawn and returning at night; moreover he often traveled incognito, personally inspecting corvée sites.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong hunted from dawn to dusk, slipped out disguised, and spied on work gangs.

sentences.zh: 侍中韋謏諫曰：「臣聞千金之子坐不垂堂，萬乘之主行不履危。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wei Su remonstrated: "Your servant has heard that the son of a thousand in gold does not sit beneath a sagging eave, nor does the lord of ten thousand chariots tread danger.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Su warned, "Princes of gold avoid risky ledges—so should an emperor avoid peril.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖天生神武，雄據四海，乾坤冥贊，萬無所慮。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty was born divinely martial, heroically holding the four seas, with heaven and earth secretly aiding—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Your star is martial and the realm kneels—heaven seconds you.

sentences.zh: 然白龍魚服，有豫且之禍；

translations.literal: Yet when the white dragon dons fish garb there is the disaster of Yu Ju;
translations.idiomatic: Yet incognito—the white dragon dressed as fish—invites fishermen's knives.

sentences.zh: 海若潛游，罹葛陂之酷，深願陛下清宮蹕路，思二神為元鑒，不可忽天下之重，輕行斤斧之間。

translations.literal: when Lord Sea swims hidden he suffers Gebei's cruelty—I deeply hope Your Majesty will clear palace avenues and halts and take the two spirits as primary mirrors—do not neglect the realm's weight and lightly walk amid axe strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Even sea gods hidden in shallows meet cruelty—clear the roads, heed those omens, never gamble the empire on stealth.

sentences.zh: 一旦有狂夫之變，龍騰之勇不暇施也，智士之計豈及設哉！

translations.literal: Once some madman strikes, the valor of Soaring Dragon guards will have no moment to deploy—could strategists' plans even be set!
translations.idiomatic: One assassin ends Soaring Dragon guards before they draw—no time for clever schemes.

sentences.zh: 又自古聖王之營建宮室，未始不于三農之隙，所以不奪農時也。

translations.literal: Moreover from antiquity sagely kings' construction of palaces never failed to use the gaps of the three farmings—thereby not stealing farm seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient builders worked only between planting seasons.

sentences.zh: 今或盛功於耘藝之辰，或煩役於收穫之月，頓斃屬途，怨聲塞路，誠非聖君仁後所忍為也。

translations.literal: Now sometimes great works press during hoeing season, sometimes burdensome corvée falls in harvest month—collapses crowd the roads and resentful voices choke the ways; truly this is not what a sage lord or benevolent heir should endure doing.
translations.idiomatic: Now you draft men at hoeing and harvest—corpses litter roads and curses fill lanes—no humane sovereign tolerates this.

sentences.zh: 昔漢明賢君也，鐘離一言而德陽役止。

translations.literal: Former Han Ming was an worthy lord—one word from Zhongli and the Deyang works ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mingdi stopped Deyang palace on one loyal sentence.

sentences.zh: 臣誠識慚昔士，言無可采，陛下道越前王，所宜哀覽。

translations.literal: Your servant truly knows shame before former scholars—his words are unworthy of adoption—yet Your Majesty's way surpasses former kings and ought pityingly to review them.
translations.idiomatic: I am no ancient worthy, yet your virtue exceeds theirs—deign to read me.

sentences.zh: 」季龍省而善之，賜以穀帛，而興繕滋繁，游察自若。

translations.literal: " Jilong reviewed it and praised it, granting grain and silk, yet construction grew ever more numerous and roaming inspections continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong praised Wei Su and paid him grain—then built faster and prowled harder.

sentences.zh: 右僕射張離領五兵尚書，專總兵要，而欲求媚于石宣，因說之曰：「今諸公侯吏兵過限，宜漸削弱，以盛儲威。

translations.literal: Right Superintendent Zhang Li, acting Masters of Writing for the Five Armies, monopolized military keys and wished to curry favor with Shi Xuan; accordingly he urged him: "Now various dukes and marquises exceed limits on clerks and troops—they ought gradually to be weakened to magnify stored awe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li, running the five-bureau army ministry, flattered Shi Xuan: "Princes hog clerks and soldiers—trim them to swell your prestige.

sentences.zh: 」宣素疾石韜之寵，甚說其言，乃使離奏奪諸公府吏，秦、燕、義陽、樂平四公聽置吏一百九十七人，帳下兵二百人，自此以下，三分置一，余兵五萬，悉配東宮。

translations.literal: " Xuan had long resented Shi Tao's favor and greatly welcomed this speech; he therefore had Li memorialize stripping the princes' clerks—Princes Qin, Yan, Yiyang, and Leping were allowed a hundred ninety-seven clerks and two hundred tent guards; below that one-third allocation; the remaining fifty thousand troops all assigned to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan, loathing Shi Tao's clout, had Zhang Li strip rival households: four great princes kept lean staffs while fifty thousand soldiers flowed to the heir's compound.

sentences.zh: 於是諸公咸怨，為大釁之漸矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princes all resented it—this became the gradual opening of great strife.
translations.idiomatic: Every prince nursed a grudge—the civil war's fuse lit.

sentences.zh: 遣征北張舉自雁門討索頭郁鞠，克之。

translations.literal: He dispatched General Who Conquers the North Zhang Ju from Yanmen to attack Suotou Yuju and overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju marched from Yanmen against Suotou Yuju and broke him.

sentences.zh: 制：「征士五人車一乘，牛二頭，米各十五斛，絹十匹，調不辦者以斬論。
