translations.literal: Regulation: "For every five levy households supply one cart, two oxen, fifteen hu of rice each, ten bolts of silk—failure to meet levy is judged capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Each quintet owed a wagon, two oxen, fifteen hu rice, ten bolts silk—default meant death.

sentences.zh: 」將以圖江表。

translations.literal: " This was in order to plan against the south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The quota fed the planned sweep south of the river.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓窮窘，鬻子以充軍制，猶不能赴，自經于道路死者相望，而求發無已。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred surnames were destitute and sold children to meet military quotas yet still could not fulfill them—those who hanged themselves along the roads stared at one another while demands for levies never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Families sold children yet missed quotas; suicides lined highways while requisitions never stopped.

sentences.zh: 會青州言濟南平陵城北石獸，一夜中忽移在城東南善石溝，上有狼狐千餘跡隨之，跡皆成路。

translations.literal: It happened that Qingzhou reported that north of Pingling city in Jinan a stone beast overnight suddenly shifted southeast of the city to Shanshi Ditch, above which wolf and fox tracks numbering over a thousand followed it, the tracks all forming roads.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou claimed a stone beast walked overnight from north of Jinan's Pingling to a southeastern ravine, tracked by a thousand wolf prints forming roads.

sentences.zh: 季龍大悅曰：「獸者，朕也。

translations.literal: Jilong greatly rejoiced and said: "The beast—that is Us.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong crowed, "The beast is me.

sentences.zh: 自平陵城北而東南者，天意將使朕平蕩江南之征也。

translations.literal: From Pingling north turning southeast—Heaven's intent is that We shall complete the campaign to level the south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Its march southeast means heaven backs my southern war.

sentences.zh: 天命不可違，其敕諸州兵明年悉集。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate cannot be resisted; order all provincial armies to assemble next year.
translations.idiomatic: Order every province to mobilize next year.

sentences.zh: 朕當親董六軍，以副成路之祥。

translations.literal: We shall personally oversee the six armies to match the auspice of the completed road.
translations.idiomatic: I will command the hosts myself to fulfill the omen.

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆賀，上《皇德頌》者一百七人。

translations.literal: " The hundred officials all congratulated him; one hundred seven persons presented "Rhapsody on August Sovereign Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers cheered; 107 scholars offered odes to his virtue.

sentences.zh: 時妖怪尤多，石然于泰山，八日而滅。

translations.literal: At that time prodigies were especially numerous—stone caught fire on Mount Tai and after eight days went out.
translations.idiomatic: Omens multiplied—Taishan stone flamed eight days.

sentences.zh: 東海有大石自立，旁有血流。

translations.literal: In Donghai a great stone stood itself upright; beside it blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai saw a megalith rise overnight, blood pooling at its foot.

sentences.zh: 鄴西山石間血流出，長十餘步，廣二尺餘。

translations.literal: Among Ye's western hills blood flowed from between stones—more than ten paces long and over two chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: West of Ye, stone seams bled a rivulet ten paces long and two chi across.

sentences.zh: 太武殿畫古賢悉變為胡，旬餘，頭悉縮入肩中。

translations.literal: Paintings of ancient worthies in the Grand Martial Hall all changed into Hu; after more than ten days their heads entirely drew back into their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Martial murals of sages morphed into Hu faces; heads sank into shoulders within a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 季龍大惡之，佛圖澄對之流涕。

translations.literal: Jilong loathed it deeply; Fotucheng wept facing them.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong shuddered; Fotucheng wept before the portraits.

sentences.zh: 甯遠劉甯攻武都狄道，陷之。

translations.literal: Ningyuan's Liu Ning attacked Wudu's Didao and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning from Ningyuan seized Didao in Wudu.

sentences.zh: 使石宣討鮮卑斛穀提，大破之，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: He sent Shi Xuan to punish Xianbei Huguti, greatly defeating him and taking thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan shattered Huguti's Xianbei, claiming thirty thousand skulls.

sentences.zh: 中謁者令申扁有寵于季龍，而宣亦昵之。

translations.literal: Palace Usher Director Shen Bian enjoyed Jilong's favor, and Xuan was also intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch chief Shen Bian charmed both throne and heir.

sentences.zh: 扁聰辯明斷，專綜機密之任。

translations.literal: Bian was clever in debate and clear in judgment, monopolizing management of secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Witty Shen Bian seized confidential authority.

sentences.zh: 季龍既不省奏案，宣荒酒內游，石韜沈湎好獵，生殺除拜皆扁所決。

translations.literal: Because Jilong no longer reviewed dossiers, Xuan drowned in wine and palace roaming while Shi Tao steeped in drink and hunting—life-and-death orders and appointments were all decided by Bian.
translations.idiomatic: With Jilong ignoring paperwork, drunken Xuan and hunt-mad Tao left promotions and executions to Shen Bian.

sentences.zh: 於是權傾內外，刺史二千石多出其門，九卿已下望塵而拜，唯侍中鄭系、王謨、常侍盧諶、崔約等十餘人與之抗禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon power tilted inside and outside—many inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials exited his gate; from the nine ministers downward men bowed to his dust—only Palace Attendants Zheng Xi, Wang Mo, Regular Attendants Lu Chen, Cui Yue, and more than ten others matched him with upright courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Power hugged Shen Bian—governors kowtowed in his courtyard—only a dozen senior advisers stood upright.

sentences.zh: 季龍又取州郡吏馬一萬四千餘匹，以配曜武關將，馬主皆復一年。

translations.literal: Jilong further took fourteen thousand-plus provincial horses to equip Yaowu barrier generals; horse owners were granted one year's remission.
translations.idiomatic: Another fourteen thousand regional mounts went to Yaowu passes; owners earned a year's tax holiday.

sentences.zh: 鎮北宇文歸執送段遼之子蘭降于季龍，獻駿馬萬匹。

translations.literal: Regional Defender of the North Yuwen Gui seized Duan Lan, son of Duan Liao, and delivered him in surrender to Jilong, presenting ten thousand fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui shipped Duan Liao's son Lan to Ye with ten thousand steppes horses.

sentences.zh: 季龍以平西張伏都為使持節、都督征討諸軍事，帥步騎三萬擊涼州。

translations.literal: Jilong appointed Pacifying-the-West Zhang Fudu commissioner with baton and commander-in-chief of all punitive expedition forces, leading thirty thousand infantry and horse to strike Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fudu took thirty thousand west against Liangzhou with full banners.

sentences.zh: 既濟河，與張駿將謝艾大戰於河西，伏都敗績。

translations.literal: Once across the Yellow River he fought Zhang Jun's general Xie Ai west of the river in great battle; Fudu suffered rout.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Yellow River Xie Ai shattered him on Liang's banks.

sentences.zh: 季龍雖昏虐無道，而頗慕經學，遣國子博士詣洛陽寫石經，校中經于秘書。

translations.literal: Although Jilong was benighted and cruel without principle, he somewhat admired classical learning, dispatching imperial-academy doctors to Luoyang to copy the stone classics and collate palace texts against them.
translations.idiomatic: For all his tyranny Jilong loved books—doctors copied Luoyang stone classics into the palace library.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒聶熊注《谷梁春秋》，列於學官。

translations.literal: Libationer of the Imperial Academy Nie Xiong annotated the Guliang commentary on Spring and Autumn and listed it among academy officers.
translations.idiomatic: Academy libationer Nie Xiong lectured on Guliang Spring and Autumn as official curriculum.

sentences.zh: 燕公石斌淫酒荒獵，常懸管而入。

translations.literal: Prince Yan Shi Bin drowned in wine and abandoned himself to hunting, often entering with pipes hung about him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi Bin of Yan drank and hunted endlessly, flutes slung like a wastrel.

sentences.zh: 征北張賀度以邊防宜警，每裁諫之。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Zhang Hedu, deeming the frontier ought to stay alert, repeatedly restrained and remonstrated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedu nagged him—border vigilance mattered.

sentences.zh: 斌怒，辱賀度。

translations.literal: Bin raged and insulted Hedu.
translations.idiomatic: Bin publicly humiliated Hedu.

sentences.zh: 季龍聞之大怒，杖斌一百，遣主書禮儀持節監之。

translations.literal: Hearing this Jilong was furious, caned Bin one hundred strokes, and dispatched Master of Documents Li Yi with baton to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong flogged him a hundred blows and posted clerk Li Yi as monitor.

sentences.zh: 斌行意自若，儀持法呵禁，斌怒殺之。

translations.literal: Bin conducted himself as before; Yi upheld law with shouted prohibitions; Bin in rage killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin shrugged; Li Yi barked regulations—Bin murdered him.

sentences.zh: 欲殺賀度，賀度嚴衛馳白之，季龍遣尚書張離持節帥騎追斌，鞭之三百，免官歸第，誅其親任十餘人。

translations.literal: He wished to kill Hedu; Hedu maintained strict guard and galloped to report it; Jilong dispatched Masters of Writing Zhang Li with baton leading horse in pursuit of Bin, flogged him three hundred strokes, dismissed him from office to his mansion, and executed more than ten of his intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Bin next aimed at Hedu; Hedu bolted to warn Jilong, who sent Zhang Li to haul Bin home, whip him three hundred times, cashier him, and kill ten favorites.

sentences.zh: 建元初，季龍饗群臣于太武前殿，有白雁百餘集于馬道南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era Jilong feasted ministers before the Grand Martial Hall when more than a hundred white geese alighted south of the horse road.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jianyuan, feasting before Grand Martial Hall, a hundred white geese settled south of the avenue.

sentences.zh: 季龍命射之，無所獲。

translations.literal: Jilong ordered them shot but nothing was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Archers bagged none.

sentences.zh: 既將討三方，諸州兵至者百餘萬。

translations.literal: When he was about to campaign against three directions, arriving provincial troops exceeded a million.
translations.idiomatic: As three-front war loomed, gathered troops passed a million.

sentences.zh: 太史令趙攬私于季龍曰：「白雁集殿庭，宮室將空，不宜行也。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan privately said to Jilong: "White geese gathering in palace courts means chambers will empty—it is inauspicious to march.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lan whispered that white geese meant hollow palaces—stay home.

sentences.zh: 」季龍納之，臨宣武觀大閱而解嚴。

translations.literal: " Jilong accepted this; he performed a grand review at Mystic Martial Watchstand and lifted martial law.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong listened, reviewed troops at Mystic Martial tower, and stood down mobilization.

sentences.zh: 以燕公斌為使持節、侍中、大司馬、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He appointed Prince Yan Bin commissioner with baton, palace attendant, grand marshal, and recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin became baton commissioner, attendant-in-chief, grand marshal, and overseer of policy.

sentences.zh: 置左右戎昭、曜武將軍，位在左右衛上。

translations.literal: He established Left and Right Martial Glory and Glorious Martial generals, ranking above Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: New ranks—Martial Glory left/right—sat above household guards.

sentences.zh: 東宮置左右統將軍，位在四率上。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace established Left and Right Commander generals, ranking above the Four Escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's compound gained commander-generals senior to the four escorts.

sentences.zh: 置上、中光祿大夫，在左右光祿上。

translations.literal: He established Senior and Middle Household Grandees, ranking above Left and Right Household Grandees.
translations.idiomatic: Senior and middle household grandees outranked ordinary grandees.

sentences.zh: 置鎮衛將軍，在車騎將軍上。

translations.literal: He established the Garrison Guard general, ranking above chariot-and-horse general.
translations.idiomatic: A new garrison guard outranked chariot commanders.

sentences.zh: 時石宣淫虐日甚，而莫敢以告。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Xuan's debauchery and cruelty grew daily worse, yet none dared report it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan's atrocities mounted—no one dared tell.

sentences.zh: 領軍王朗言之于季龍曰：「今隆冬雪寒，而皇太子使人斫伐宮材，引于漳水，功役數萬，士眾籲嗟。

translations.literal: Leader of the Army Wang Lang spoke to Jilong saying: "Now deep winter snow is cold, yet the imperial heir sends men to fell palace timber and haul it to Zhang River—works number tens of thousands and soldiers sigh.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Lang reported that the crown prince drafted tens of thousands to drag palace timber to the Zhang River in blizzard cold.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜因游觀而罷之也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to take advantage of an excursion to halt it.
translations.idiomatic: Cancel it on inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 」季龍如其言。

translations.literal: " Jilong did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong complied.

sentences.zh: 既而宣知朗所為，怒欲殺之而無因。

translations.literal: Presently Xuan learned Lang had done this and raged, wishing to kill him yet lacked cause.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan learned Wang Lang meddled and burned to kill him—without pretext.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守房，趙攬承宣旨言于季龍曰：「昴者，趙之分也，熒惑所在，其主惡之。

translations.literal: When Mars guarded the Fang mansion Zhao Lan, carrying Xuan's intent, spoke to Jilong saying: "The Mao asterism is Zhao's allotment; wherever Mars dwells its lord suffers evil.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars parked in Fang, Zhao Lan—doing Xuan's bidding—said Mao marked Zhao's fate and Mars brought doom.

sentences.zh: 房為天子，此殃不小。

translations.literal: Fang represents the Son of Heaven—this calamity is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Fang houses the sovereign—ominous indeed.

sentences.zh: 宜貴臣姓王者當之。

translations.literal: A noble minister surnamed Wang ought to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: A minister surnamed Wang must absorb it.

sentences.zh: 」季龍曰：「誰可當者？

translations.literal: " Jilong said: "Who can bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Who counts? asked Jilong.

sentences.zh: 」攬久而對曰：「無復貴于王領軍也。

translations.literal: " Lan after a long while replied: "None are nobler than Household Commander Wang.
translations.idiomatic: After silence Zhao Lan named Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 」季龍既惜朗，且猜之，曰：「更言其次。

translations.literal: " Jilong cherished Lang yet also suspected him, saying: "Speak the next choice.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctant to lose Wang Lang yet wary, Jilong demanded an alternate.

sentences.zh: 」攬曰：「其次唯中書監王波耳。

translations.literal: " Lan said: "Next is none other than Palace Secretariat Supervisor Wang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Next choice: Wang Bo, palace secretariat chief.

sentences.zh: 」季龍乃下書追波前議遣李宏及答楛矢之愆，腰斬之，及其四子投于漳水，以厭熒惑之變。

translations.literal: " Jilong thereupon issued an edict blaming Wang Bo for his earlier counsel sending Li Hong and answering with hawthorn arrows; he cut Bo at the waist and together with his four sons cast them into Zhang River to appease Mars's mutation.
translations.idiomatic: He retroactively condemned Wang Bo for the Li Hong affair, halved him at the waist, drowned his four sons in the Zhang, and called it penance for Mars.

sentences.zh: 尋湣波之無罪，追贈司空，封其孫為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he pitied Bo's innocence, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works, and enfeoffed his grandson as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Remorse came quickly: Wang Bo was canonized minister of works and a grandson received a fief.

sentences.zh: 平北尹農攻慕容皝凡城，不克而還。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Yin Nong attacked Murong Huang's Fancheng but failed to take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Nong, general who pacifies the north, struck Murong Huang at Fancheng, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 黜農為庶人。

translations.literal: He degraded Nong to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Nong was stripped to commoner.

sentences.zh: 時白虹出自太社，經鳳陽門，東南連天，十餘刻乃滅。

translations.literal: At that time a white rainbow emerged from Grand Soil Altar, crossed Fengyang Gate, linked southeast to heaven, and after more than ten ke vanished.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow shot from the soil altar through Fengyang Gate to the horizon—visible many minutes.

sentences.zh: 季龍下書曰：「蓋古明王之理天下也，政以均平為首，化以仁惠為本，故能允協人和，絹熙神物。

translations.literal: Jilong issued an edict saying: "In general ancient enlightened kings' ordering of the realm took equitable governance as foremost and humane transformation as root—thereby they harmonized human hearts and brightened numinous things.
translations.idiomatic: His edict preached balance and mercy as the ancient kings had.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇薄，君臨萬邦，夕惕乾乾，思遵古烈，是以每下書蠲除徭賦，休息黎元，庶俯懷百姓，仰稟三光。

translations.literal: We, insignificant and slight, face the myriad regions with fearful vigilance night and day, wishing to follow ancient fierce virtue—therefore whenever We issue edicts remitting corvée and taxes and resting the black-haired folk, We hope below to embrace the hundred surnames and above to obey the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed humility and cited tax breaks meant to comfort subjects and please heaven.

sentences.zh: 而中年已來變眚彌顯，天文錯亂，時氣不應，斯由人怨於下，譴感皇天。

translations.literal: Yet since mid-reign anomalies have grown ever plainer—astronomy disordered and seasonal qi unresponsive—this follows from resentment below moving august heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-reign omens—skewed stars, broken seasons—he blamed on popular hatred alarming heaven.

sentences.zh: 雖朕之不明，亦群後不能翼獎之所致也。

translations.literal: Although Our lack of clarity shares blame, it also stems from various regional lords unable to aid and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Petty kings failed him too, he admitted.

sentences.zh: 昔楚相修政，洪災旋弭；

translations.literal: Formerly Chu ministers repaired policy and vast floods soon ceased;
translations.idiomatic: Chu ministers once ended floods by reform.

sentences.zh: 鄭卿厲道，氛祲自消，皆服肱之良，用康群變，而群公卿士各懷道迷邦，拱默成敗，豈所望於台輔百司哉！

translations.literal: Zheng ministers sternly upheld the way and miasmic vapors vanished of themselves—all were capable arms of state who used health to settle mass changes—yet now dukes and ministers each harbor the Way yet lose the state, folding hands in silence over success or failure—is this what We expect of terrace ministers and hundred offices!
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's stern ministers cleared foul air—today's cowards betray every hope.

sentences.zh: 其各上封事，極言無隱。

translations.literal: Let each submit sealed memorials speaking to the utmost without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Demand blunt sealed advice.

sentences.zh: 」於是閉鳳陽門，唯元日乃開。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he closed Fengyang Gate, opening it only on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang Gate stayed shut except New Year.

sentences.zh: 立二畤於靈昌津，祠天及五郊。

translations.literal: He erected two suburban altars at Lingchang Ford sacrificing to heaven and the five suburban gods.
translations.idiomatic: Twin altars rose at Lingchang Ford for heaven and the five-direction rites.

sentences.zh: 李壽以建寧、上庸、漢固、巴征、梓潼五郡降于季龍。

translations.literal: Li Shou surrendered five commanderies—Jianning, Shangyong, Hangu, Bazheng, and Zitong—to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou handed over five Shu commanderies to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 先是，季龍起河橋於靈昌津，採石為中濟，石無大小，下輒隨流，用功五百餘萬而不成。

translations.literal: Earlier Jilong had begun a river bridge at Lingchang Ford, quarrying stone for midstream piers—whatever the stone's size, once lowered it followed the current; five hundred thousand man-days brought no success.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred thousand labor-days sank stone that the current swept away—no bridge.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣使致祭，沈璧於河。

translations.literal: Jilong dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice and sink a jade disk in the river.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed and drowned a ritual jade in the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 俄而所沈譬流於渚上，地震，水波騰上，津所殿觀莫不傾壞，壓死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Soon the sunk jade floated to a sandbar; earthquake struck and waves surged—every hall and lookout at the ford collapsed; more than a hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: The jade resurfaced; quake and surge flattened the ford buildings—over a hundred died.

sentences.zh: 季龍恚甚，斬工匠而止作焉。

translations.literal: Jilong was furious beyond measure, executed the craftsmen, and halted the works.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the builders and abandoned the bridge.

sentences.zh: 命石宣、石韜，生殺拜除皆迭日省決，不復啟也。

translations.literal: He ordered Shi Xuan and Shi Tao—life, death, appointments, and dismissals all alternately reviewed daily without further memorial consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan and Shi Tao rotated daily power over appointments and executions—no need to ask Ye.

sentences.zh: 司徒申鐘諫曰：「度賞刑威，後皇攸執，名器至重，不可以假人，皆以防奸杜漸，以示軌儀。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Shen Zhong remonstrated: "Measuring rewards and fearful punishments is what later sovereigns grasp; instruments of rank are supremely weighty and may not be lent others—all to guard against treason at inception and display normative ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong warned that rewards and terror belong on the throne alone.

sentences.zh: 太子國之儲貳，朝夕視膳而不及政也。

translations.literal: The heir is the state's reserve heir—morning and evening he attends meals yet does not touch governance.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs attend parents at meals, not policy.

sentences.zh: 庶人邃往以聞政致敗，殷鑒不遠，宜革而弗遵。

translations.literal: Commoner Sui formerly brought ruin by hearing governance—the bronze mirror is not distant; reform ought to replace blind obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui's ruin proved heirs must not rule.

sentences.zh: 且二政分權，鮮不及禍。

translations.literal: Moreover divided twin authority seldom escapes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Split power invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 周有子頹之釁，鄭有叔段之難，此皆由寵之不道，所以亂國害親，惟陛下覽之。

translations.literal: Zhou had the disaster of Prince Tui; Zheng had the crisis of Shuduan—all followed from improper favor and thereby disordered the state and harmed kin—may Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Zitui and Zheng's Shuduan warn what indulgence costs.

sentences.zh: 」季龍不從。

translations.literal: " Jilong did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong ignored him.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事孫珍問侍中崔約曰：「吾患目疾，何方療之？

translations.literal: Eastern Palace Superintendent Sun Zhen asked Palace Attendant Cui Yue: "We suffer eye ailment—what remedy?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen asked Cui Yue for an eye cure.

sentences.zh: 」約素狎珍，戲之曰：「溺中則愈。

translations.literal: " Yue, accustomed to rib Zhen, jested: "Soak them in urine and they heal.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue joked: bathe them in urine.

sentences.zh: 」珍曰：「目何可溺？

translations.literal: " Zhen said: "How can eyes soak in urine?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen asked how eyes could steep in piss.

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「卿目睕々，正耐溺中。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Your eyes are sunk deep—just right for soaking in urine.
translations.idiomatic: Cui answered that deep-set sockets were perfect for the treatment.

sentences.zh: 」珍恨之，以白宣。

translations.literal: " Zhen hated him and reported it to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen told Shi Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣諸子中最胡狀，目深，聞之大怒，誅約父子。

translations.literal: Among Xuan's sons he was most Hu in appearance with deep eyes; hearing this he was furious beyond measure and executed Yue father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan—deepest eyes, most barbarian face—murdered the Cui clan.

sentences.zh: 珍有寵于宣，頗預朝政，自誅約之後，公卿已下憚之側目。

translations.literal: Zhen enjoyed Xuan's favor and broadly intervened in court policy; after executing Yue, from dukes and ministers downward all feared him and viewed him askance.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen dominated court business until officials flinched at his shadow.

sentences.zh: 季龍子義陽公鑒時鎮關中，役煩賦重，失關右之和。

translations.literal: Jilong's son Prince Yiyang Shi Jian then garrisoned Guanzhong; corvée multiplied and taxes grew heavy, losing harmony west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi Jian of Yiyang held Guanzhong while crushing taxes bred hatred.

sentences.zh: 其友李松勸鑒，文武有長髮者，拔為冠纓，余以給宮人。

translations.literal: His friend Li Song urged Jian: among civil and military men with long hair, pull it for hat tassels and give the remainder to palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song proposed shaving officials' long hair for hat cords and sending locks to harem weavers.

sentences.zh: 長史取發白之，季龍大怒，以其右僕射張離為征西左長史、龍驤將軍、雍州刺史以察之，信然，征鑒還鄴，收松下廷尉，以石苞代鎮長安。

translations.literal: The chief clerk reported it in memorial; Jilong was furious beyond measure, appointed his Right Superintendent Zhang Li as Western Expedition Left Chief Clerk, Grand General Who Soars Like a Dragon, and Inspector of Yongzhou to investigate—finding it true, summoned Jian back to Ye, seized Song and handed him to commandant-in-chief, and substituted Shi Bao to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial exposure infuriated Jilong; Zhang Li verified the hair scheme, recalled Shi Jian, jailed Li Song, and posted Shi Bao to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 發雍、洛、秦、并州十六萬人城長安未央宮。

translations.literal: He mobilized one hundred sixty thousand people from Yong, Luo, Qin, and Bing to wall Chang'an's Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred sixty thousand builders raised walls around Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 季龍性既好獵，其後體重，不能跨鞍，乃造獵車千乘，轅長三丈，高一丈八尺，罝高一丈七尺，格獸車四十乘，立三級行樓二層於其上，克期將校獵。

translations.literal: Jilong by nature loved hunting; afterward his body grew heavy and he could not straddle the saddle—therefore he built a thousand hunting carts with shafts three zhang long, height one zhang eight chi, spring-trap nets one zhang seven chi high, forty beast-grid carts, erecting three-tier marching towers of two levels atop them, setting dates for commanders to hunt in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Too fat to ride, he commissioned a thousand hunting chariots—three-zhang poles, spring nets, paired towers—for staged battues.

sentences.zh: 自靈昌津南至滎陽，東極陽都，使御史監察，其中禽獸有犯者罪至大辟。

translations.literal: From Lingchang Ford south to Xingyang, east to Yangdu, he had censors supervise; any who harmed the hunt's beasts faced capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Censors patrolled a vast game preserve from Lingchang to Xingyang—touching royal quarry meant death.

sentences.zh: 御史因之擅作威福，百姓有美女好牛馬者，求之不得，便誣以犯獸論，死者百餘家，海岱、河濟間人無寧志矣。

translations.literal: Censors thereby arrogated authority and favor—when commoners had beautiful women or fine oxen and horses but denied requests, they falsely accused them of offending the hunt—more than a hundred households died; between sea and Dai, Yellow River and Ji no man knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: Censors framed hundreds for "poaching" to seize wives and herds—Huai to sea knew no rest.

sentences.zh: 又發諸州二十六萬人修洛陽宮。

translations.literal: He further mobilized two hundred sixty thousand men from various provinces to repair Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred sixty thousand more rebuilt Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 發百姓牛二萬餘頭配朔州牧官。

translations.literal: He confiscated more than twenty thousand commoners' oxen to assign to Shuzhou pasture officials.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand private oxen went to Shuzhou herds.

sentences.zh: 增置女官二十四等，東宮十有二等，諸公侯七十餘國皆為置女官九等。

translations.literal: He added twenty-four grades of female officers; twelve grades for the Eastern Palace; more than seventy ducal and marquisal states each received nine grades of female officers.
translations.idiomatic: The harem grew twenty-four female ranks; twelve for the heir; seventy feudal courts gained nine ranks each.

sentences.zh: 先是，大發百姓女二十已下十三已上三萬餘人，為三等之第以分配之。

translations.literal: Earlier he had massively drafted commoners' daughters below twenty sui and above thirteen—more than thirty thousand—in three ranked classes for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He had pressed thirty thousand teen girls into three beauty tiers.

sentences.zh: 郡縣要媚其旨，務於美淑，奪人婦者九千餘人。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties fawning on his intent strove for beauty and grace—those who seized others' wives numbered more than nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates stole over nine thousand wives to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 百姓妻有美色，豪勢因而脅之，率多自殺。

translations.literal: Commoners' wives of fine looks powerful houses then coerced—most committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Many beautiful wives killed themselves rather than enter barracks.

sentences.zh: 石宣及諸公又私令采發者，亦垂一萬。

translations.literal: Shi Xuan and various princes moreover privately ordered recruiters—again nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' private impress gangs took another ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 總會鄴宮。

translations.literal: All assembled at Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: The harvest of women packed Ye.

sentences.zh: 季龍臨軒簡第諸女，大悅，封使者十二人皆為列侯。

translations.literal: Jilong faced the gallery reviewing and ranking the girls, greatly pleased, enfeoffing twelve envoys all as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong graded concubines from a balcony and made twelve recruiters full marquises.

sentences.zh: 自初發至鄴，諸殺其夫及奪而遣之縊死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: From first levy to arrival at Ye those who killed husbands or took wives and drove them to hang themselves numbered more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand women died—murdered husbands or suicide—before reaching Ye.

sentences.zh: 荊、楚、揚、徐間流叛略盡，宰守坐不能綏懷，下獄誅者五十餘人。

translations.literal: Between Jing, Chu, Yang, and Xu wanderers and rebels were nearly exhausted; shepherds and guards seated for inability to soothe faced prison and execution—more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty southern magistrates died for failing to calm refugee waves.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫逯明因侍切諫，季龍大怒，遣龍騰拉而殺之。

translations.literal: Household Grandee with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Lu Ming remonstrated sharply while attending; Jilong was furious beyond measure and dispatched Soaring Dragon guards to drag and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ming's blunt lecture earned dismemberment by Soaring Dragon guards.

sentences.zh: 自是朝臣杜口，相招為祿仕而已。

translations.literal: From this court ministers sealed their mouths, merely inviting one another to salary posts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials clammed up—office became a paycheck.

sentences.zh: 季龍常以女騎一千為鹵簿，皆著紫綸巾、熟錦褲、金銀鏤帶、五文織成靴，游于戲馬觀。

translations.literal: Jilong constantly used a thousand female riders as his halberd escort—all wearing purple silk kerchiefs, brocade trousers, gold-and-silver openwork belts, and five-pattern woven boots—roaming at Playhorse Watch.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand horsewomen in purple headcloths and brocade filled his processions to Playhorse Watch.

sentences.zh: 觀上安詔書五色紙，在木鳳之口，鹿盧回轉，狀若飛翔焉。

translations.literal: Above the watch edicts of five-color paper were mounted in a wooden phoenix's mouth; pulleys spun so it seemed to fly.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts unfurled from a mechanical phoenix beak on colored paper.

sentences.zh: 遣涼州刺史麻秋等伐張重華。

translations.literal: He dispatched Inspector of Liang Ma Qiu and others to campaign against Zhang Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu marched on Zhang Chonghua of Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃軌與中黃門嚴生不協，會大雨霖，道路陷滯不通，生因而譖軌不修道，又訕謗朝政，季龍遂殺之。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Zhu Gui and Inner Yellow Gate Yan Sheng were incompatible; when prolonged heavy rain bogged and blocked roads, Sheng therefore slandered Gui for not repairing ways and also mocked court governance—Jilong thereupon executed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Yan Sheng blamed minister Zhu Gui for rain-ruined roads and "slander"—Jilong executed Gui.

sentences.zh: 於是立私論之條，偶語之律，聽吏告其君，奴告其主，威刑日濫，公卿已下，朝會以目，吉凶之問，自此而絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established statutes on private opinion and laws against whispered speech, allowing clerks to denounce lords and slaves to denounce masters—punishments grew daily excessive; from dukes and ministers downward court meetings used only eyes—questions of fortune and woe ceased from this.
translations.idiomatic: He legalized informers—clerks on lords, slaves on masters—until colleagues communicated only with glances.

sentences.zh: 軌之囚也，冠軍苻洪諫曰：「臣聞聖主之馭天下也，土階三尺，茅茨不翦，食不累味，刑措而不用。

translations.literal: When Gui was imprisoned, General Who Vanquishes the Vanguard Fu Hong remonstrated: "Your servant has heard that sagely sovereigns rein the realm with earthen steps three chi high, thatched roofs untrimmed, meals without doubled flavors, punishments set aside unused.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong, as Zhu Gui sat in chains, praised frugal sage-kings.

sentences.zh: 亡君之馭海內也，傾宮瓊榭，象箸玉杯，截脛剖心，脯賢刳孕，故其亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: Ruined sovereigns rein the seas within with leaning palaces and jade terraces, ivory chopsticks and jade cups, cutting shins and carving hearts, drying worthies and ripping pregnant women—therefore their fall came swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Tyrants built crystal towers and carved up counselors—speeding collapse.

sentences.zh: 今襄國、鄴宮足康帝宇，長安、洛陽何為者哉？

translations.literal: Now Xiangguo and Ye palaces suffice to roof the emperor's cosmos—what purpose Chang'an and Luoyang?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguo and Ye already palace enough—why twin western capitals?

sentences.zh: 盤于游田，耽於女德，三代之亡恆必由此。

translations.literal: Obsessed with roaming hunts and drowned in women's charms—the falls of the Three Ages always followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: Hunts and harems ended every dynasty.

sentences.zh: 而忽為獵車千乘，養獸萬里，奪人妻女，十萬盈宮。

translations.literal: Yet suddenly a thousand hunting carts, beasts nurtured across ten thousand li, wives and daughters seized until a hundred thousand fill the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Now you pen game across a continent and pack palaces with stolen women.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃軌，納言大臣，以道路不修，將加酷法，此自陛下政之失和，陰陽災沴，暴降霖雨七旬，霽方二日，縱有鬼兵百萬，尚未及修之，而況人乎！

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Zhu Gui, speaking minister, faced cruel law merely because roads went unrestored—this follows from Your Majesty's governance losing harmony; yin-yang disaster brought ninety days of rain—clear skies only two days—even a million ghost soldiers could not finish repairs—how much less mortal men!
translations.idiomatic: Blaming Zhu Gui for rains that stalled roadworks ignores seventy days of storms clearing barely two days—not legions could pave that fast.

sentences.zh: 刑政如此，其如史筆何！

translations.literal: With punishments and governance thus, what of the historians' brush!
translations.idiomatic: How will histories judge this?

sentences.zh: 其如四海何！

translations.literal: What of the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: What will the realm say?

sentences.zh: 特願止作徒，休宮女，赦硃軌，允眾望。

translations.literal: We specially hope you will halt convict laborers, release palace women, pardon Zhu Gui, and satisfy popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Stop corvée, free girls, spare Zhu Gui—that is what people crave.

sentences.zh: 」季龍省之不悅，憚其強，但寢而不納，弗之罪也。

translations.literal: " Jilong reviewed it unhappily yet dreaded Hong's strength—only shelved it without adopting but did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong scowled, feared Fu Hong too much to punish, and tabled the memo.

sentences.zh: 乃停二京作役焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he halted construction labor at the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did halt building at the twin capitals.
